## [2.49.97] - 2026-05-22

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Flatten the initiative-tracker wrapper card so its contents (summary, GM Controls, init entries) read as independent cards floating on the map — same vibe as the roll log.** User-requested follow-up to v2.49.95 (transparent sidebar). The `.gm-panel` wrapper around `#initiative-panel` had its own background, border, and shadow, which made the whole initiative tracker look like one big card sitting on top of the transparent drawer. The user wanted it to behave like the Roll Log — each entry is its own card, gaps between them show the map. v2.49.97 drops the wrapper's card styling on `#initiative-panel` specifically (other `.gm-panel` instances unchanged), and hoists the wrapper's old card treatment up onto the summary header so it still reads as a visually anchored section header. Everything below the summary already has its own backgrounds — the GM Controls box has a border + shadow, each `.init-entry` has its own border + bg + shadow, the simpler `.init-row` view does too. Pure CSS; no behavior, endpoint, broadcast, or schema change.
**Description:** One CSS edit in `app/templates/tabletop.html`. Added a `#initiative-panel` block (and `#initiative-panel > summary` + `#initiative-panel[open] > summary` siblings) just below the existing `.gm-panel:not([open]) .init-panel-chevron` rule. The new rules: (a) `#initiative-panel { background: transparent; border: none; box-shadow: none; border-radius: 0; overflow: visible; }` — removes the wrapper card. (b) `#initiative-panel > summary { border: 1px solid rgba(167,139,250,.35); border-radius: 8px; box-shadow: 0 3px 14px rgba(0,0,0,.22); }` — hoists the wrapper's card styling onto the summary. (c) `#initiative-panel[open] > summary { border-bottom-color: rgba(167,139,250,.35); margin-bottom: 8px; }` — overrides the generic `.gm-panel[open] > summary` accent-color bottom border (would orphan a connector to nothing once the wrapper is gone) and adds 8 px gap below the summary so the content cards aren't flush against it.
**Description (cont):** Why scoped to `#initiative-panel` specifically. The other GM-Tools / Battle drawer panels (encounters, templates, music, roll request, etc.) still benefit from looking like single cards because their bodies don't contain independently-styled sub-cards — flattening them would leave naked content floating without visual anchor. The initiative tracker is the exception: every item in its body is ALREADY its own card (GM Controls box has border + shadow + own gradient header; `.init-entry` / `.init-row` items have bg + border + shadow + margin-bottom 4px between them). So removing JUST the initiative wrapper exposes the inner cards as already-finished UI — no further restyling needed.
**Description (cont 2):** Why keep the summary styled as a card. With the wrapper gone, if the summary kept only its gradient gradient (no border, no radius, no shadow), it would visually drift between "section header" and "floating widget". Giving it the same border + radius + shadow the wrapper used to have keeps it clearly anchored as a section divider above the content cards. The summary's existing gradient background fills the rounded rectangle nicely; no other visual changes needed.
**Description (cont 3):** Why drop the accent bottom-border when open. The shared `.gm-panel[open] > summary { border-bottom-color: var(--accent); }` rule painted a 2 px accent stripe under the summary to visually connect it to the content body inside the wrapper. With the wrapper gone, that connector now points into transparency — looks like an orphaned underline. Overriding to the same border color as the rest of the summary's outline turns it into a normal closed border, which reads as a complete card.
**Description (cont 4):** What still sits between cards. After this commit, the user sees: (a) summary card (rounded, gradient bg, full border + shadow), (b) 8 px gap = map shows through, (c) GM Controls box (if GM) (rounded, border + shadow, own gradient header), (d) `.gm-panel-body` padding (8 px each side, 12 px bottom — that wraps the battle banner + init list), (e) the battle banner if active, (f) each init entry / row, each its own bordered card with 4 px margin-bottom showing the map between them. Same general pattern the roll log uses.
**Description (cont 5):** Test coverage. Pure CSS visual change; the Playwright canvas + multi-target chat suites (5 tests in `tests/harness_ui/`) all still green, confirming no JS / DOM regression. Manual verification path: open the Battle tab, confirm the summary now looks like a standalone card with the same chunky border as before; toggle it open/closed to confirm the chevron + border behavior; spawn Tavern Brawl and confirm map shows between each combatant card.
**Description (cont 6):** Verification. Curl `/version` confirms v2.49.97 live. Existing harness tests pass.

### Changed
- `app/templates/tabletop.html::#initiative-panel` (NEW CSS rules) — wrapper card flattened to transparent / no-border / no-shadow / no-radius / overflow: visible. Summary picks up the wrapper's old card styling (border + radius + shadow) and overrides the generic `.gm-panel[open] > summary` accent-bottom-border + adds an 8 px margin-bottom for breathing room. Scoped to the initiative panel only; other `.gm-panel` instances (encounters, music, roll request, etc.) unchanged.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** No behavior, endpoint, or schema changes. Pure visual layout.
- **Visual change.** The initiative wrapper card is replaced by a standalone summary card + naked content underneath. Each init entry already had its own card styling so they remain readable.
- **Other `.gm-panel` instances unaffected.** Encounters, templates, music, roll request, and all other expandable panels in the Battle / GM Tools drawers keep their existing wrapper-card appearance.

## [2.49.96] - 2026-05-22

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Drawer UX polish: Characters splits off into its own tab, tab buttons match the Ruler button styling, and action-economy chips inline with the init/HP row to save vertical space.** Three coordinated tweaks on the right-side drawer. (1) The Characters mini-sheet card stack used to share the Battle drawer with the initiative tracker, which made the Battle tab heavy and pushed the init tracker below the fold once 3-4 PCs were assigned. Characters now lives in a dedicated `#characters-drawer` panel reachable via a new "Characters" tab between Battle and GM Tools. The same `#player-chars-panel` + `#player-char-list` ids ride along so the JS at `tabletop.html:3119` (renderPlayerCharList) and the WS hp_update handler at `:3892` keep binding correctly. (2) `.drawer-tab-btn` styling adopts the `.canvas-tool-btn` (Ruler) look: 36 px min-height, padding 6 × 12, font-size 12, hover = `var(--bg-2)` surface + accent border, active = solid accent fill. The topbar now reads as one consistent tool/tab row instead of two visually disconnected button groups. (3) The action-economy chip strip (Act / Bns / Rxn / Movement) inside each init-tracker mini-header used to stack on its own row underneath the Init/HP stat line. With v2.49.96 the chips share a wrapping flex row with the stat text, saving ~24 px per combatant — three combatants on a typical 1080p browser reclaims ~72 px which fits an extra entry above the fold. Buff chips stay on their own row beneath since they need the breathing room for end-buff × buttons.
**Description:** Five file edits, all in `app/templates/tabletop.html`. **(1)** `.drawer-tab-btn` + `.drawer-tab-btn:hover` + `.drawer-tab-btn.active` CSS rules — rewritten to mirror `.canvas-tool-btn` (the Ruler button). Same min-height, padding, border, radius, font-size, letter-spacing, transition. Hover swaps to `var(--bg-2)` + accent border; active fills with `var(--accent)` and white-on-accent text. (2) `.drawer-tab-bar` HTML — added a fourth tab button between Battle and GM Tools: `<button class="drawer-tab-btn" data-target="characters-drawer">Characters</button>`. The drawer-system JS at `:2974` picks it up automatically via `document.querySelectorAll('.drawer-tab-btn')`. (3) Extracted the entire `<details id="player-chars-panel">...</details>` block out of the `<div id="players-drawer">` body and wrapped it in a new `<div id="characters-drawer" class="drawer-panel"><div class="drawer-body">...</div></div>` sibling. The inner panel content (the details summary + the #player-char-list div + the Jinja for-loop over characters) is byte-for-byte unchanged. (4) New CSS class `.mini-header-stats` — flex row with `align-items: center; gap: 8px; flex-wrap: wrap; margin-top: 2px`. Holds the init/HP `<span class="mini-header-sub">` + the `${economyChips}` block. Nested `.mini-header-sub` and `.econ-chips` both get `margin-top: 0` overrides since the parent row handles the spacing. (5) The `init-entry` template literal in the renderBattle function (`:5212` region) — wrapped the existing `<div class="mini-header-sub">...</div>${economyChips}` pair in a new `<div class="mini-header-stats"><span class="mini-header-sub">...</span>${economyChips}</div>`. The HP-update JS still finds `.mini-header-sub` and rewrites its text; no JS change needed.
**Description (cont):** Why a new tab for Characters specifically. The Battle drawer had three things crammed in: the init tracker (huge — combatants + GM controls + add-from-map + manual-add panel + roll-init), the optional sound mini-panel for non-GMs, and the Characters mini-sheet stack (5-8 cards × ~120 px each). At 1080p with 4 PCs, the GM scrolling past the init tracker to reach the Characters panel becomes friction. Peeling Characters into its own tab puts both surfaces one click apart and lets each get full vertical room. The id `#player-chars-panel` is preserved so the v2.1.5 GM-sees-all-PCs semantics + the v2.3.16 mini-sheet partial keep working without code edits.
**Description (cont 2):** Why tabs were restyled. v2.49.94 added the Ruler button in the topbar's right cluster, and v2.49.95 polished the sidebar drawer overlay. The remaining inconsistency was the drawer tabs: 5 × 11 px padding, font-size 11, color fg-mute — visually noisier and less tap-friendly than the 36 × ~60 px Ruler button next to them. Matching the canvas-tool-btn style unifies the topbar's rightmost cluster as one tool/tab row and lifts the tabs to the same 44/36 px touch target the CLAUDE.md guideline recommends for compact panels. The mobile-narrow override at `:1269` (padding 6 × 10) still kicks in unchanged for sub-768 px viewports.
**Description (cont 3):** Why action-economy chips moved inline. The init-tracker mini-header was: token portrait, name on row 1, "Init X · HP Y/Z" on row 2, "○ Act ○ Bns ○ Rxn 0/30 ft" on row 3, then optional buff chips on row 4. Three or four stacked rows per combatant ate vertical real estate fast; with auto-rolling Tavern Brawl (6+ combatants) the tracker was scrolling-heavy even on a 1080p browser. Putting Init/HP + econ chips on ONE wrapping row keeps both visible at-a-glance and saves ~24 px per combatant. The chips wrap to a new line on narrow drawer widths (the user could shrink the sidebar below 480 px in a future commit), so legibility is preserved on phone-sized contexts.
**Description (cont 4):** Why the buff chips DIDN'T also get inlined. The buff chips have `×` end-buff buttons that need ~24 px tap targets each, and individual buff names can be wide ("Hunter's Mark", "Sneak Attack +3d6"). Putting them on the same row as the econ chips would cause aggressive wrapping that visually fragments the stat line. Buff chips already render conditionally (empty list = no row, no padding), so combatants without active buffs already only get 1-row stats with this commit. With buffs active, the buff row is the second row — still tighter than the pre-commit 3-row layout.
**Description (cont 5):** Test coverage. The Playwright canvas suite + chat-card multi-target suite (5 tests total in `tests/harness_ui/`) all still green, confirming no regression in pan / drag / multi-target rendering. No new test for this commit — the changes are pure visual layout that's hard to assert robustly without pixel-diff testing. Manual verification path: open the demo tabletop, confirm the four tabs (Roll Log, Battle, Characters, GM Tools for the GM) render with the same chunky-button look as the 📏 Ruler button; switch to Characters and confirm the mini-sheet card stack scrolls inside its dedicated drawer; spawn the Tavern Brawl encounter and confirm each combatant in the init tracker shows Init/HP + econ chips on a single wrapping row.
**Description (cont 6):** Verification. Curl `/version` confirms v2.49.96 live. Existing harness tests pass (no contract changes; CSS + DOM tweaks only).

## [2.49.95] - 2026-05-22

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Push tokens, portraits, and presence pills BEHIND the drawer sidebar via `z-index: 50` on `.drawer-sidebar`.** User-reported regression from v2.49.94's transparent-sidebar overlay. With the sidebar absolute-positioned and no z-index, the map-pane's positioned children (`#vtt-canvas` z-index:1, `#gif-token-overlay` z-index:2, `#presence-bubbles` z-index:3) escaped their parent's stacking context and rendered ON TOP of the sidebar. Cards in the drawer were visually layered behind the tokens, which made character portraits cover roll-log entries and looked like the cards were "behind" the map. Fix is one line: set `.drawer-sidebar { z-index: 50 }` so the whole sidebar (and its children — drawer-panel, gm-panel cards, roll-log entries) renders above the canvas + every token overlay. The ruler-picker hint (z-index 210) and AoE picker preview (z-index 200) stay on top of the sidebar — those are cursor-following overlays that center on the map and don't visually conflict with the sidebar's right edge.
**Description:** One CSS edit in `app/templates/tabletop.html::.drawer-sidebar`. Added `z-index: 50` to the existing block (which already had `position: absolute; top: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; width: 480px; background: transparent`). Inline comment explains why 50 — above the canvas/overlay z-stack (1–3) but below the ruler/AoE banners that intentionally float over everything. Pure visual fix; no behavior, endpoint, broadcast, or schema change.
**Description (cont):** Why z-index 50 specifically. The map-pane's children use z-index 1, 2, and 3. The ruler hint uses 210 (defensive against the AoE picker's 200). Picking 50 leaves comfortable headroom above the token stack (so a future Phase-3F token overlay at z-index 4 still stays behind the sidebar) without touching the deliberately-elevated cursor-follow overlays. Below 4 would risk a token overlay climbing back over the sidebar; above 200 would mean the sidebar covers the ruler hint, which is wrong because the hint is meant to confirm a measurement in progress.
**Description (cont 2):** Why this didn't show up in the v2.49.94 Playwright canvas tests. The tests assert that the canvas transform mutates on right-click drag — they don't probe paint order or visual layering. Visual regressions like z-index conflicts are exactly the class that requires either pixel-diff screenshot testing or human eyeballs; the v2.49.94 commit didn't catch it because the canvas pan + drag mechanics still work fine (the user can still pan + drag through the gaps between cards). Filed below: a Playwright pixel-snapshot test for the drawer overlay would catch this class of regression, but the current suite intentionally avoids pixel-diff because it's notoriously brittle across font/AA differences between local + CI.
**Description (cont 3):** Verification. (a) Existing `test_tabletop_canvas.py` still green — pan + drag unaffected by the new z-index. (b) Existing `test_attack_toast_multi_target.py` still green — the .roll-toast container floats outside the sidebar entirely. (c) Manual: open the demo tabletop with bandits + PC tokens spawned, swap to the Roll Log drawer, fire a multi-target attack — tokens visible in the gaps between roll-log cards, no tokens overlapping the cards themselves.

### Fixed
- `app/templates/tabletop.html::.drawer-sidebar` — added `z-index: 50` so tokens / gif overlay / presence pills render behind the sidebar's cards. Closes the v2.49.94 visual regression.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure CSS one-liner; no behavior change.
- **What still sits on top of the sidebar.** The ruler picker hint (centered floating pill, z-index 210) + the AoE picker preview (z-index 200). Both are cursor-anchored to the map's interior and shouldn't visually overlap the right-edge sidebar in practice, but if they DO they correctly draw on top.

### Filed
- **Playwright pixel-snapshot test for the drawer layout** — would catch z-index regressions like the v2.49.94 → v2.49.95 cycle. Skipped today because pixel-diff tests are notoriously flaky across font + AA differences between local + CI environments; revisit if the cycle repeats.

## [2.49.94] - 2026-05-22

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Drawer-sidebar UX polish — transparent backdrop so the map shows through the gaps between cards, Roll Request renamed to GM Roller, and the roll-log Clear button moved into the GM Roller header.** Three related sidebar tweaks: (1) the right-side drawer that hosts Roll Log / Battle / GM Tools now floats over the right edge of the map with a transparent backdrop, so the map is visible in the inter-card gaps inside every panel; (2) the "📋 Roll Request" sub-panel inside the Roll Log drawer is renamed to "📋 GM Roller" since it does more than just request rolls (it's the GM's dice-roll launchpad); (3) the "🗑 Clear" button that used to live in the Roll Log header is moved into the GM Roller summary, decluttering the roll-log card stream. Cards inside the drawer (gm-panel cards, .roll-card entries, the Dice Roller box) retain their opaque backgrounds — only the empty space between them goes transparent. User-requested UX polish; no behavior change to any endpoint, broadcast, or schema. Pure CSS + HTML.
**Description:** Four file edits in `app/templates/tabletop.html`. **(1)** `.tabletop-layout` — added `position: relative` so the absolute-positioned sidebar anchors against it (instead of the viewport). (2) `.drawer-sidebar` — switched from flex-row layout participation (`flex-shrink: 0; width: 480px; background: var(--bg-2); border-left: 1px solid var(--border)`) to absolute overlay (`position: absolute; top: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; width: 480px; background: transparent`). The map-pane's `flex: 1` now expands to the full width of `.tabletop-layout` since the sidebar is removed from the flex flow. (3) `.drawer-panel` — backdrop changed from `var(--bg-2)` to `transparent` so the gaps INSIDE each panel show through. (4) `.gm-panel` — added `background: var(--bg-2)` so each card retains an opaque backdrop independent of the now-transparent parent panel.
**Description (cont):** Also: removed the entire roll-log header div (`<div>... <strong>ROLL LOG</strong> <button id="roll-log-clear-btn">🗑 Clear</button></div>`) since (a) the rolls stream is self-evidently a roll log, and (b) the Clear button moved. Re-added the Clear button inside the GM Roller `<summary>` element, alongside the existing 📋 GM Roller header + "GM only" badge. The button's onclick has `event.stopPropagation()` so clicking it doesn't toggle the parent `<details>` open/close. ID `#roll-log-clear-btn` is unchanged — the JS listener at `tabletop.html:2987` still binds correctly. The "Roll Request" text inside the same `<summary>`'s `<h4>` is renamed to "GM Roller".
**Description (cont 2):** Why the sidebar overlays the map instead of just having a transparent background. If only the background was changed, the page's body color (`var(--bg)`) would show through the gaps — not the map. The user explicitly said "see the map between the cards", which requires the sidebar to be ON TOP of the map-pane visually. Absolute positioning achieves this: the map-pane fills the full width of `.tabletop-layout`, the sidebar floats over its right 480 px, and the inter-card empty space inside the sidebar lets the map peek through.
**Description (cont 3):** Why .gm-panel needed an explicit background. Before this commit, .gm-panel had `border: 1px solid rgba(167,139,250,.35)` + a shadow but NO `background-color` — it relied on the parent .drawer-panel's `var(--bg-2)` showing through its open card body. Once the parent went transparent, the body became transparent too, and content like the init-tracker rows lost their readable backdrop. Adding `background: var(--bg-2)` to the card itself restores legibility while keeping the inter-card gap transparent. The .roll-card class (roll log entries) already had `background: var(--bg)` so no fix needed there.
**Description (cont 4):** Why the Clear button moves to GM Roller specifically. Per the user's request. The original button was visible to ALL players (the local-clear semantics — "only affects your view, server history unchanged" — make sense for any user). The new location is inside the `{% if is_gm %}`-gated GM Roller block, so non-GM players no longer see the Clear button. This is a minor regression for player UX (filed below); the user explicitly named the GM Roller as the destination, so honoring the literal request takes priority. If player Clear access becomes important, the button could be lifted into the always-visible Dice Roller card directly above the GM Roller details.
**Description (cont 5):** Why "GM Roller" instead of "Roll Request". The panel does more than request rolls from players — it has Save / Check mode toggles, a DC picker, ability-targeted quick buttons, a per-player target picker, and a visibility selector. "GM Roller" frames it as the GM's primary dice-launcher console, which matches its actual function. The id `#roll-request-panel` is unchanged for backward-compat with any JS that targets it (and to keep the v2.49.85-and-prior diffs grep-able).
**Description (cont 6):** Test coverage. Pure-CSS visual changes don't have a test. The Playwright canvas suite (test_tabletop_canvas.py) confirms the map still loads + the right-click pan still mutates the canvas transform after the sidebar becomes an overlay — the absolute positioning could in principle have shifted the canvas mousedown geometry; the canvas-pan test running green proves it didn't. The chat-card multi-target suite (test_attack_toast_multi_target.py) also still green, confirming the .roll-toast container's anchoring outside the sidebar wasn't affected. Manual verification path: open the tabletop, swap between Roll Log / Battle / GM Tools tabs and confirm the map peeks through between cards in each panel; verify the Clear button is visible inside the GM Roller summary and clicking it doesn't toggle the parent `<details>`.

### Changed
- `app/templates/tabletop.html::.tabletop-layout` — added `position: relative`.
- `app/templates/tabletop.html::.drawer-sidebar` — `position: absolute; right: 0`, `background: transparent`, removed `border-left`.
- `app/templates/tabletop.html::.drawer-panel` — `background: transparent`.
- `app/templates/tabletop.html::.gm-panel` — added `background: var(--bg-2)`.
- `app/templates/tabletop.html::#roll-log-drawer` — removed the header `<div>` containing the old Clear button + "ROLL LOG" label.
- `app/templates/tabletop.html::#roll-request-panel > summary` — renamed "📋 Roll Request" → "📋 GM Roller"; appended the moved `#roll-log-clear-btn` button with `event.stopPropagation()` on click.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** No endpoint / broadcast / schema changes. JS listener at `#roll-log-clear-btn` still binds correctly (id preserved). The id `#roll-request-panel` is unchanged.
- **Visual change.** Right-side drawer is now an overlay over the right edge of the map. Map-pane is now full-width inside `.tabletop-layout`; the sidebar floats over its right 480 px.

### Filed
- **Non-GM Clear button** — moving the button into the GM-gated GM Roller block hides it from non-GM players. If player Clear access matters, lift the button into the always-visible Dice Roller card (just above the GM Roller `<details>`) instead.

## [2.49.93] - 2026-05-22

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Chat card now renders per-target attack + damage toasts for multi-target weapon attacks — closes the v2.49.85 filed item.** When `/attack` fires with `target_combatant_ids: [a, b, c]`, the server's `weapon_attack` broadcast has carried an `auto_attack_targets` list since v2.49.85 (one entry per per-target outcome). The client's `roll_toast.js` WS handler only read the primary target's top-level fields, so a 3-bandit Multiattack rendered as if it hit only Bandit Alpha — the secondary + tertiary fresh rolls landed in the roll log but never surfaced as toasts. v2.49.93 fans the chain out: when `auto_attack_targets.length >= 2`, the handler iterates the list and renders one attack-d20 toast + one damage toast per per-target outcome, staggered 700 ms apart so they don't pile on each other. The existing 1600 ms attack→damage gap is preserved inside each chain. For 3 targets the full sequence runs ~3.0 seconds; each toast self-dismisses after 10 s per the existing fade. Single-target attacks (0 or 1 entries in `auto_attack_targets`) keep the legacy top-level field rendering — backward compat is byte-for-byte unchanged. New tests in `tests/harness_ui/test_attack_toast_multi_target.py` exercise both paths via Playwright.
**Description:** Two file edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/static/roll_toast.js` — extracted the per-target rendering into a local helper `_renderOutcome(outcome, attackOffsetMs)` that takes a per-target dict + an offset; the existing single-target branch now wraps the top-level fields in that same shape and calls the helper at offset 0. New branch when `auto_attack_targets.length >= 2`: iterate the list, call `_renderOutcome` with `idx * 700` offset. (2) `tests/harness_ui/test_attack_toast_multi_target.py` (NEW, 2 tests) — Playwright suite that boots a 3-bandit battle, POSTs `/attack` with a 3-element list, then asserts 6 `.roll-toast` elements render with every bandit name in at least one label. Second test pins the single-target backward-compat path. Both tests close with a teardown that resets the campaign battle to empty so subsequent suite tests don't trip on left-behind combatants. (3) `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — new section for the multi-target tests + a NOTE explaining the pre-existing `test_attack_toast.py` failures are unrelated to this commit.
**Description (cont):** Why the 700 ms stagger. Single-target rendering already uses a 1600 ms gap between the attack d20 toast + the damage toast — to let the dice spin animation (~1.5 s) finish before the damage dice start spinning. For multi-target, firing every target's attack at t=0 would have all N d20 toasts spinning simultaneously — visually busy and the player can't tell which die belongs to which target. 700 ms stagger between targets means each target's attack toast arrives, lands, and starts its own 1600 ms countdown to its damage toast before the next target's attack even fires. The total wall-clock for 3 targets is (3-1)*700 + 1600 = 3000 ms before the last damage lands, which fits comfortably inside the 10 s auto-dismiss window. For 5+ targets the chain extends but each toast still has > 4 s of visible time after landing.
**Description (cont 2):** Why not a consolidated single card with per-target rows. Two reasons. (a) Consistency: single-target rendering already uses the existing dice-toast UI (the `.roll-toast` element with `.rt-label` / `.rt-dice` / `.rt-bonus` / `.rt-sum`). A consolidated multi-target card would need a new visual style + new CSS + new tests — much larger scope. (b) Information density: a consolidated card would compress 3 d20s into one row of mini-icons + 3 damage numbers in a stacked list, which loses the animation feedback that makes the existing toast satisfying. Per-target chains preserve the existing UX 1:1, just N times. The consolidated-card design is filed for a future commit if user feedback requests it.
**Description (cont 3):** Backward-compat preserved. Three guarantees. (a) When `auto_attack_targets` is empty (untargeted attack, e.g. an unprovoked swing-at-air), the legacy branch runs and the top-level damage fields fire one toast (no attack toast since there's no target_ac to roll against). (b) When `auto_attack_targets` has exactly 1 entry (legacy single-target via `target_combatant_id` — see `test_attack_legacy_single_target_emits_one_entry` in the HTTP+WS harness), the legacy branch still runs and uses the top-level fields. (c) The fired toast payload shape (`{expression, total, breakdown, note, user_id, user_name, char_name}`) is unchanged in both paths. `showRollToast` itself is not modified. The .atk-strike click handler in `sheet_dnd5e.html` (which directly calls `window.showRollToast(...)` on the response body, bypassing the WS handler) also unchanged.
**Description (cont 4):** Per-target target_name format. Each `auto_attack_targets[i].target_name` is the combatant's display name (e.g. "Bandit Alpha"). The toast's existing `→ TARGET` suffix renders correctly for every entry in the list. AC + HIT/MISS/CRIT verdicts use the per-target `target_ac` / `hit` / `is_crit` fields. Damage suffix (`−N HP · X → Y HP · ☠ dead`) uses the per-target `damage_applied` / `target_hp_before` / `target_hp_after` / `target_dead` / `target_dying`. All fields are populated by the server's v2.49.85 per-target loop.
**Description (cont 5):** Pre-existing test failures in `test_attack_toast.py` (unrelated). The two existing UI tests (`test_pip_shortsword_strike_fires_roll_toast` + `test_tavik_warhammer_strike_fires_roll_toast`) currently fail because the click handler in `sheet_dnd5e.html` pops the v2.16.0 Sneak Attack uplift modal (Pip is a Rogue Lv 1+) BEFORE reaching the fetch, and the test never dismisses the modal. This regression has been there since v2.16.0 — not introduced by v2.49.93. Tracked in the Filed section + the coverage doc. The fix is small (the test should click `#up-cancel` to dismiss the uplift modal before asserting the toast) but conceptually separate from the chat-card rendering work; filing for a follow-up commit so the version bump stays a single coherent change.
**Description (cont 6):** Verification. (a) `pytest tests/harness_ui/test_attack_toast_multi_target.py -v` — both new tests pass. (b) `pytest tests/harness_ui/test_tabletop_canvas.py -v` — all 3 v2.49.92 canvas tests still pass (regression check that the refactor didn't touch IIFE behavior). (c) `pytest tests/harness_ui/test_smoke.py -v` — the 2 sheet-load smoke tests pass. (d) The HTTP+WS harness is unaffected — this is a pure client-side refactor; tests at `tests/harness/` would only have caught a server-side broadcast-shape change which didn't happen. (e) Manual: not yet performed; the Playwright tests give equivalent coverage. (f) Rebuild + curl `/version` confirms v2.49.93 live on port 8013.

### Added
- `app/static/roll_toast.js` — `weapon_attack` WS handler now renders one attack+damage chain per per-target outcome when `auto_attack_targets.length >= 2`. Closes the v2.49.85 filed "Chat card multi-target rendering" item.
- `tests/harness_ui/test_attack_toast_multi_target.py` (NEW) — 2 Playwright tests gating the new behavior + the single-target backward-compat path.
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — entry for the new test file + a note on the pre-existing `test_attack_toast.py` breakage.

### Changed
- `app/static/roll_toast.js::message handler::weapon_attack` — refactored into a `_renderOutcome(outcome, attackOffsetMs)` helper; single + multi-target call sites both delegate. Pure refactor in the single-target path (no behavior change).

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Single-target attacks (`auto_attack_targets` is 0 or 1 entries) render identically to pre-v2.49.93 — the legacy top-level fields drive the chain. The `.atk-strike` direct-call path on the character sheet is unchanged.
- **Wall-clock for N targets.** ~(N-1)*700 + 1600 ms from the first attack toast to the last damage toast. Toast auto-dismiss is 10 s; up to 5 targets fit cleanly inside that window before earlier toasts begin to fade.

### Filed
- **Pre-existing test_attack_toast.py failures** — both tests have been silently failing since v2.16.0 (uplift modal blocks .atk-strike's fetch). Fix: prepend a `#uplift-modal #up-cancel` dismissal in the test, or seed an empty class-features list for Pip in the demo. Tracked here so a follow-up commit can land in isolation.
- **Consolidated multi-target chat card** — alternative UI where a single `.roll-toast` shows all targets in a stacked grid (vs the current N separate chains). Defer until user feedback requests it.
- **Per-target uplift detection** — Hex / Hunter's Mark / Colossus Slayer still only apply to the primary target. Filed from v2.49.85.
- **Per-target range check** — multi-target attacks only range-check the primary. Filed from v2.49.85.

## [2.49.92] - 2026-05-22

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Fix the actual root cause of broken pan + token drag: `_hoverCursor` was in the temporal dead zone when `render()` first ran, crashing the tabletop IIFE — and the canvas listeners were silently never attached.** Lands the browser-level test harness (Playwright) the user explicitly asked for, which made the bug instantly diagnosable. v2.49.88 (CSS) and v2.49.90 (selectstart JS) were red herrings — they didn't introduce pan/drag breakage, they just touched code adjacent to the real cause. The real bug landed in v2.49.81 (Phase 3B hover rangefinder): `_hoverCursor` was used inside the body of `function render()` (line 1680ish), but the `let _hoverCursor = null;` declaration sat ~900 lines below in the "Drag handling" section (line 2197). `render()` is invoked at IIFE startup (line 1915), well before the declaration is reached, which hits JavaScript's `let` temporal-dead-zone rule and throws `ReferenceError: Cannot access '_hoverCursor' before initialization`. That throw aborts the rest of the IIFE — the `canvas.addEventListener('mousedown', …)` registration ~40 lines later never executes, neither do mousemove / mouseup / wheel / contextmenu / keydown / etc., neither do the `window.vtt*` global exports. Result: the canvas accepts no clicks, no drags, no pan, no token movement. The error logs to the browser console as a pageerror, but the user just sees a dead canvas. Two doc-only "fixes" (v2.49.88 CSS, v2.49.90 selectstart) and one revert each later, this was finally pinned by writing the Playwright test that loads `/campaign/1` and asserts `window.vttGetCharacters` exists (it didn't, until the fix). Restores end-to-end canvas interaction on every browser including iPad. The iPad text-select issue stays a separate concern — it never broke pan/drag; v2.49.88 was wrongly blamed; both fix-attempts will be retried under the new harness.
**Description:** Two file edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/static/tabletop.js` — moved `let _hoverCursor = null;` from line 2197 (inside the "Drag handling" section) to line 1244 (immediately before `function render()` is defined). render() now sees the binding hoisted from the closure scope, no TDZ. The comment block moved with it; added a v2.49.92 supplementary comment explaining WHY the declaration must sit there and pointing forward readers at the harness test that pins the placement. (2) `app/version.py` + `README.md` + this changelog file — version bump. (3) NEW: `tests/harness_ui/test_tabletop_canvas.py` — three Playwright tests against the demo tabletop: `test_tabletop_loads_without_js_errors` (no pageerrors during IIFE setup), `test_right_click_drag_pans_canvas` (right-mouse drag mutates `canvas.style.transform`), `test_left_click_drag_moves_token` (left-mouse drag on a token persists a new world-space position through `/api/campaign/{cid}/token/{id}/move`).
**Description (cont):** Why this bug went undetected for 11 versions (v2.49.81 → v2.49.91). Three reasons. (a) The IIFE crash is silent at the layout level — the canvas + the GIF overlay + the topbar all render fine. Only on first interaction does the user notice "the canvas isn't responding"; until then it looks like a working tabletop. (b) The error logs as a console pageerror, which neither the existing HTTP+WS harness nor any prior UI test was reading. (c) Manual testing always involves clicking around almost immediately — but if your last cached page state shows a non-zero `panX`/`panY` from before v2.49.81, the canvas might still appear panned-correctly on reload via `localStorage`-restored state even though pan-from-input is broken. Combined, the bug was invisible from the dev's normal workflow.
**Description (cont 2):** Why the Playwright tests catch it. The first test (`test_tabletop_loads_without_js_errors`) registers a `page.on("pageerror", …)` handler before navigating. The TDZ ReferenceError fires during the IIFE; the handler captures it; the assert at the bottom rejects any non-empty error list. The second + third tests independently exercise pan + drag, both of which fail noisily if the canvas mousedown listener was never registered. Even if a future commit muffles the ReferenceError or reroutes it, the pan/drag asserts will still fire because they observe the OBSERVABLE end-state of the canvas (transform + persisted token position), not the absence of an exception.
**Description (cont 3):** Why the test harness lands as part of this commit, not a separate one. The tests are what diagnosed the bug — they ARE the diagnostic instrument. Splitting them into a separate commit would mean either (a) ship the harness alone first as v2.49.92, watch it fail loudly in CI, ship the fix as v2.49.93 (two commits, one with red CI), or (b) write the harness against the broken baseline + assert "broken behavior is broken" as a pinning test, which inverts the right contract. The cleaner shape is "ship the test + the fix together, prove the test catches the regression by referencing the prior commit, and from this commit forward CI runs the test on every push." Per CLAUDE.md's "one conceptually-distinct change = one commit" rule, the conceptual change here IS "make canvas interaction work and guard it with a test" — those two parts are inseparable because the test caused the diagnosis.
**Description (cont 4):** Why v2.49.88 + v2.49.90 were red herrings. v2.49.88 added CSS (user-select: none + -webkit-touch-callout: none) to .map-pane + #vtt-canvas. None of those properties block mousedown / pointerdown event delivery per spec, and they don't in practice — pan was already broken by the v2.49.81 IIFE crash, the user just noticed it AFTER v2.49.88 because that's the version they tested. v2.49.89 reverted the CSS but didn't address the IIFE crash, so pan stayed broken. v2.49.90 added a `selectstart` listener; same story — the listener registration was DOWNSTREAM of the canvas mousedown listener in the IIFE, so v2.49.90's lines never executed either, but the user testing v2.49.90 saw still-broken pan and reasonably blamed the new commit. v2.49.91 reverted v2.49.90. All four commits (88, 89, 90, 91) churned over a symptom (the missing iPad text-select fix + the pan regression) while the actual cause sat unmodified at line 2197. This commit closes the loop.
**Description (cont 5):** Verification path. Steps: (a) `git stash` the tabletop.js change to restore the v2.49.91 broken baseline. (b) Run `pytest tests/harness_ui/test_tabletop_canvas.py -v` — would fail on `test_tabletop_loads_without_js_errors` with "JS errors on tabletop load: ['Cannot access _hoverCursor before initialization', ...]" + on the pan + drag tests with "no transform change". (c) `git stash pop` to re-apply the fix. (d) Re-run — all three tests pass. Skipped (b) in the actual landing path because rebuilding the broken container would leave the user blocked again mid-verification; the diagnostic step was performed during development against an in-memory pre-fix tabletop.js. (e) CI: the existing `harness-ui` GitHub Action runs `tests/harness_ui/` on every push + PR; the new test file lands inside that directory and will run automatically.
**Description (cont 6):** Coverage-doc update. `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` gains three rows under a new "Tabletop canvas" section for the three new tests. Total test count bumps by +3.

### Fixed
- `app/static/tabletop.js` — `let _hoverCursor = null;` hoisted from line 2197 to line 1244, BEFORE `function render()` is defined. Eliminates the temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError that aborted the IIFE on every tabletop page load since v2.49.81. Pan + token drag + every `window.vtt*` global export now actually register.

### Added
- `tests/harness_ui/test_tabletop_canvas.py` (NEW, 3 tests, ~250 lines) — Playwright suite for canvas interactions. Catches the v2.49.81-class regression: any future change that breaks pan, drag, or the IIFE itself fails CI before merge.
  - `test_tabletop_loads_without_js_errors` — registers `pageerror` listener, navigates to the tabletop, asserts no JS exceptions during load.
  - `test_right_click_drag_pans_canvas` — drives right-mouse drag inside the visible .map-pane, asserts the canvas's CSS transform's translate(...) component shifted by > 20 px.
  - `test_left_click_drag_moves_token` — resets a known token (Pip) to a known on-screen position via `/token/{id}/move?override=true`, then drives left-mouse drag on the canvas, asserts the token's persisted x/y mutated by at least one grid cell.
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — three new entries; total bumped by +3.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure JS hoist + new test file; no behavior changes for users beyond "the tabletop works again". CSS untouched (the v2.49.88 + v2.49.90 changes were already reverted; baseline is v2.49.87 state).
- **iPad text-select still open.** Now under the protection of the new test harness — any future attempt at the fix must keep all three pan/drag/load tests green to merge. That's the safety net the original two attempts lacked.

### Filed
- **iPad Magic Keyboard text-select** (third attempt) — defer until the harness has had a few days of green CI to confirm stability. When re-attempted, the fix MUST keep the three new tests passing; that's the explicit gate.

## [2.49.91] - 2026-05-22

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Revert v2.49.90 — JS `selectstart` listener didn't fix the iPad text-select issue and map manipulation is still broken on both desktop and iPad.** Second revert of an iPad text-select attempt. User-reported: pan + token drag still broken at v2.49.90. The selectstart listener was meant to be event-narrower than v2.49.88's CSS approach (which blocked all kinds of gestures); turns out something about it ALSO interacts badly with the canvas event pipeline. Rather than keep guessing at the right minimal fix, revert to the v2.49.89 baseline (== v2.49.87 behavior) and shift focus to building the test infrastructure user explicitly requested: a Playwright-style browser harness that can simulate canvas pan / drag and catch this class of regression BEFORE it ships. The iPad text-select issue remains open until a future commit can verify the fix in that harness.
**Description:** One edit — removed the v2.49.90 `_blockSelectStart` helper + the two `addEventListener('selectstart', …)` registrations in `app/static/tabletop.js`. The code block sat between the right-click-pointer handlers and the "Drag handling" comment block; that whole block is now gone, restoring the exact v2.49.89 / v2.49.87 state of the file at that location.
**Description (cont):** Why a clean revert rather than patching. Two attempts (CSS v2.49.88, JS selectstart v2.49.90) have failed to fix the iPad issue AND both ended up breaking pan / drag in ways that weren't predicted from the spec. The right move is to stop guessing, restore the working baseline, build the test harness that would have caught both regressions instantly, and then attempt the fix again with that safety net in place.
**Description (cont 2):** What probably went wrong with v2.49.90's selectstart. Best guess from the post-mortem: `selectstart` fires synchronously DURING `mousedown` event dispatch on canvas elements. In Safari (and possibly some Chromium versions), calling `preventDefault()` on the synchronous selectstart can interact with the `mousedown`'s internal "begin pointer capture" routine — which is what pan / drag rely on for the subsequent mousemove deliveries to land on the right element. The spec doesn't require this coupling, but real-world browser implementations have it. Per CLAUDE.md the conservative path on a user-blocking regression is "revert first, theorize later."
**Description (cont 3):** Why the user-requested test harness comes next. The user explicitly asked "please create tests to identify these kinds of issues during devlopment." The HTTP+WS pytest suite can't reach canvas event handlers — these are pure-frontend gestures that need a real browser to drive. The next commit adds a Playwright-based browser test that loads the tabletop page, simulates right-click drag (pan) + left-click drag (token drag), and asserts that pan/drag observably mutate the page state. Once that test exists and passes on the v2.49.91 baseline, it becomes the gate for any future iPad text-select attempt — if the test fails, the change doesn't ship.
**Description (cont 4):** Verification. The edit is an exact inverse of v2.49.90's tabletop.js diff. Diff against v2.49.89 should show only the version + changelog edits, not any tabletop.js change. Manual: open tabletop in desktop browser, confirm pan (right-drag) + token drag (left-drag on owned token) work.

### Fixed
- Reverted v2.49.90's `selectstart` listener from `app/static/tabletop.js`. Restores v2.49.89 baseline so the user is unblocked.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Two pure-additive lines + a 3-line helper removed; no other behaviors share the selectstart path in this file. Suite-wide tests unaffected (the pure-frontend gesture handling was never harness-covered to begin with).
- **iPad text-select still open.** Won't be re-attempted until the next commit lands the test harness that can verify a fix doesn't re-break pan / drag.

### Filed
- **Build a browser-level test harness (Playwright)** for canvas gestures — next commit. The harness must minimally cover: (a) right-click pan changes the `panX` / `panY` globals, (b) left-click drag on an owned token mutates token coords and emits `token_move`, (c) the page loads without console errors. Future iPad-fix commits gate their merge on this harness passing.

## [2.49.90] - 2026-05-22

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Block the iPadOS Magic Keyboard text-select gesture via a JS `selectstart` handler.** Second attempt at the v2.49.88 issue. v2.49.88 tried CSS (`user-select: none` + `-webkit-touch-callout: none` on `#vtt-canvas` + `.map-pane`) and was reverted in v2.49.89 because it broke map panning on both iPad and desktop. This commit takes a more surgical approach: a JS `selectstart` event listener on `#vtt-canvas` and `.map-pane` that calls `preventDefault()`. The browser fires `selectstart` immediately before it starts a text-selection drag; preventing it cancels only the selection gesture, leaving every other event (mousedown, pointerdown, touchstart, contextmenu, wheel) to deliver normally. Pure JS, no CSS — so the v2.49.88 regression cannot recur. The token labels iOS Live Text was latching onto stay canvas-drawn (no DOM change); the gesture is simply aborted before iOS escalates it into a selection rect. Doc-only edit (one helper function + two `addEventListener` calls); no harness coverage because iPad-trackpad behavior can't be simulated by the HTTP+WS suite.
**Description:** One file edit, in `app/static/tabletop.js` just after the existing right-click `pointerdown` listeners. Added a `_blockSelectStart(ev)` helper that calls `ev.preventDefault()`, then registered it on `selectstart` for both `mapPane` and `canvas`. Placed near the v2.21.2 / v2.47.2 iPad-trackpad block so future maintainers can see the full iPad-quirk handling cluster in one place.
**Description (cont):** Why `selectstart` and not `user-select: none`. v2.49.88 demonstrated that the CSS approach has bad interactions with the existing `touch-action: none` + pan-handler stack — exactly which property is the culprit isn't pinned down (best guess from the v2.49.89 post-mortem: `-webkit-touch-callout: none` blocks iOS's secondary-tap → contextmenu pipeline that desktop right-click-pan depends on). The `selectstart` JS handler avoids ALL of that: it doesn't change layout, doesn't change pointer-events delivery, doesn't change touch-action semantics, doesn't change focus behavior. The browser fires `selectstart` synchronously before it commits to a selection; `preventDefault()` aborts that single gesture and only that gesture.
**Description (cont 2):** Why on BOTH `mapPane` AND `canvas`. The selectstart event bubbles from the deepest target up to `document`. Registering on both adds belt + suspenders: even if the user's drag begins outside the canvas (e.g. on the gif-token-overlay, the presence-pill area, the map-bg-layer img) but inside `.map-pane`, the parent listener catches it. The two listeners are redundant in the common case but cheap (one function ref, two registrations).
**Description (cont 3):** Why no harness test. The behavior is iOS-only and depends on actual hardware (Magic Keyboard trackpad on iPad Pro). The HTTP+WS harness can't simulate iPadOS gesture pipelines. Per CLAUDE.md the every-endpoint-needs-a-test rule covers HTTP endpoints / WS broadcast shapes — this commit adds neither, only changes client-side gesture handling. Manual verification is the validation path: user to confirm on their iPad Pro + Magic Keyboard that (a) the text-select callout no longer activates on token drag AND (b) map panning still works on both iPad and desktop.
**Description (cont 4):** Verification. Static review: the change is a 10-line addition in a well-isolated region of `tabletop.js`. No other behaviors share the selectstart event path in this file. Existing harness suite (~339 tests) is unaffected because it's a pure-frontend change. User to verify the iPad behavior on hardware; if it still leaks through, the next attempt would intercept `dragstart` / `gesturestart` in similar fashion.

### Fixed
- `app/static/tabletop.js` — new `_blockSelectStart` helper + two `selectstart` listeners on `#vtt-canvas` + `.map-pane`. Blocks the iPad Magic Keyboard trackpad's text-selection / Live Text gesture without touching CSS or other event handlers.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure-additive client JS. Other browsers either don't fire `selectstart` (Firefox) or fire it harmlessly (Chrome / Safari desktop where there's no text to select on the canvas anyway). No CSS changes — the v2.49.88 regression that v2.49.89 reverted cannot recur.
- **User-reported.** Magic Keyboard trackpad text-select activation on token drag, second attempt after v2.49.88 failed + v2.49.89 reverted.

### Filed
- **`dragstart` / `gesturestart` interception** — if `selectstart` alone doesn't fully suppress the iPad Live Text gesture on this hardware/iOS combo, the next attempt would call `preventDefault` on `dragstart` (HTML5 drag-and-drop) and `gesturestart` (iOS pinch/rotate). Both are non-overlapping with the existing mousedown / touchstart / pointerdown handlers. Defer until user confirms whether this commit closes the issue.

## [2.49.88] - 2026-05-22

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Block iPadOS Magic Keyboard text-select gesture on the tabletop canvas.** User-reported. When dragging tokens on the canvas with the Magic Keyboard trackpad, iPadOS was activating the system text-selection callout (lookup / share / copy) instead of starting the token drag. Cause: `#vtt-canvas` + `.map-pane` had `touch-action: none` (which only blocks scroll/zoom) but didn't opt out of the separate text-selection / touch-callout gestures that the trackpad pipeline routes through. Fix: add `-webkit-user-select: none`, `user-select: none`, and `-webkit-touch-callout: none` to both elements. Three properties, applied symmetrically. Mirrors the existing pattern on `.presence-pill` / `.mini-header` / other interactive bits that already opt out. Doc-only CSS edit; no behavior change on non-iOS browsers (those rules already evaluate to a no-op when there's no text content to select).
**Description:** Two CSS edits in `app/templates/tabletop.html`. **(1)** `.map-pane` — added the three properties alongside the existing `touch-action: none`. (2) `#vtt-canvas` — same three properties. Mac and Linux browsers ignore `-webkit-touch-callout` (vendor prefix only applies on iOS WebKit), so the change is iOS-targeted in effect even though the CSS ships universally. The `user-select: none` pair (un-prefixed + `-webkit-` prefix) also suppresses accidental text-selection on desktop browsers that interpret a long-drag as a selection — net-positive there too.
**Description (cont):** Why all three properties. `-webkit-touch-callout: none` is iOS-only and specifically blocks the long-press / force-touch lookup callout. `user-select: none` (W3C standard) blocks text-selection drags in modern browsers. `-webkit-user-select: none` is the legacy prefix Safari + older iOS WebKit still respect (current iOS Safari is mostly W3C-compliant but older Magic Keyboard firmware + older iPadOS versions accept only the prefixed form). Belt + suspenders + back-compat-belt.
**Description (cont 2):** Why `touch-action: none` alone wasn't enough. The CSS `touch-action` property specifically governs the GESTURES the browser allows to act on an element (scroll, zoom, pinch). It does NOT cover iOS's separate text-selection pipeline (which is treated as a UI-level system gesture, not a browser-level touch action). The Magic Keyboard trackpad routes click-drag through that text-selection pipeline by default when the underlying element is plausibly "text-containing" — which a canvas with default `user-select: text` (the user-agent default) qualifies as.
**Description (cont 3):** Why no harness coverage. The behavior is iOS-only and depends on actual hardware (Magic Keyboard trackpad). The HTTP+WS harness can't simulate iPadOS gesture pipelines; even Playwright can't drive the iPad's Magic Keyboard trackpad meaningfully. Manual verification on the affected device is the validation path.
**Description (cont 4):** Verification. The user reported the regression; CSS change pushed to v2.49.88. User to verify on their iPad Pro + Magic Keyboard combo (should now drag tokens cleanly without the text-select callout interrupting).

### Fixed
- `app/templates/tabletop.html::.map-pane` — added `-webkit-user-select: none`, `user-select: none`, `-webkit-touch-callout: none`.
- `app/templates/tabletop.html::#vtt-canvas` — same three properties.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure CSS additions. Other browsers (Mac/Linux/Windows) ignore the `-webkit-` prefixed rules; the unprefixed `user-select: none` is widely supported + harmless on non-touch devices (canvas + map-pane don't host selectable text anyway).
- **User-reported.** Magic Keyboard trackpad text-select activation on token drag.

Tapping a row toggles it; the new "Confirm (N)" button at the bottom commits all picks at once. The first picked combatant rides through the legacy singular fields (so single-pick still works server-side); 2+ picks add `target_combatant_ids` for the v2.49.85 multi-target loop. **Description:** Two edits. **(1)** `app/templates/sheet_dnd5e.html::_promptTargetPicker` — new `allowMulti` opt (default true). When true, each row gets a `.target-picker-check` span (the visual checkbox), `aria-pressed` toggles on click, the picked set accumulates in JS, and the new `.target-picker-confirm` button commits all picks. When false (legacy callers can opt out), the old single-tap-to-pick path runs. (2) CSS additions for `.target-picker-row.is-multi`, the green-checked `:where([aria-pressed="true"])` state, the checkbox spec (18px square, green when checked, ✓ glyph), and the Confirm button's prominent-when-enabled / dim-when-empty style. **Description (cont):** Why default `allowMulti: true`. The TODO described multi-select as the primary use case. Existing callers that expected single-tap behavior would break in principle, but in practice EVERY existing caller in the codebase invokes `_promptTargetPicker` from the attack-flow where multi-target is the right semantic. The opt-out parameter handles future single-tap needs (e.g. a "set the Hex target" flow where exactly one target is required). Trading one default-flip for cleaner mobile UX.
**Description (cont 2):** Why the checkbox visual rather than just `aria-pressed`-with-color. Accessibility + glanceability. A checkbox is a universal "select me" affordance; users instantly know what tapping a row does. Color-only state (green-tinted row) reads as "highlighted" but doesn't communicate "this is going into the multi-select bag." The 18-px square with a `✓` when checked is a textbook list-pick UI; no learning curve.
**Description (cont 3):** Why the Confirm button is dim until at least one pick. A "Confirm (0)" button that fires on tap would be ambiguous — does it mean "skip" or "submit empty selection"? The dim+disabled state is clearer: "you haven't picked anything yet, this button doesn't do anything." Skip + Cancel are still available for the empty-set + abort intents.
**Description (cont 4):** Why ride the first picked combatant through the legacy singular fields when picked.size === 1. Server's v2.49.85 multi-target loop reconciles either form (singular OR list) into the same internal state. But the CHAT CARD on the front end reads the singular fields for the headline "Pip → Bandit Alpha" rendering. Until that learns about `auto_attack_targets`, sending only the list would leave the chat card showing "no target" for a single-pick. Belt + suspenders: legacy fields populated AND the list when 2+ picks.
**Description (cont 5):** Verification. Manual: opened Pip's character sheet on a mobile-sized viewport, clicked an attack button while no targets were set → modal opened with checkbox rows + the dim Confirm button. Tapped two rows → Confirm became "Confirm (2)" + active-green. Tapped Confirm → modal closed + attack fired against both bandits (server logs showed two `weapon_attack` broadcasts with fresh per-target rolls in `auto_attack_targets`). Skip still works (returns empty body); Cancel still works (returns null + aborts attack). Smoke + attack regression: 17 tests pass.

### Changed

- `app/templates/sheet_dnd5e.html` CSS — new `.target-picker-row.is-multi`, `.target-picker-check`, `.target-picker-confirm` rules.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Existing callers that need single-tap behavior can pass `{allowMulti: false}`. Server-side single-target contract unchanged. Existing 339 harness tests + v2.49.85 multi-target tests pass.
- **TODO closed.** The v2.49.79 "Targeting Button on the Attack Flow" item is done end-to-end: server (v2.49.85) + canvas client (v2.49.86) + modal picker (this commit).

## [2.49.85] - 2026-05-22

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **`/attack` accepts a multi-target list — server side of the v2.49.79 targeting-button TODO.** New body field `target_combatant_ids: list` in addition to the existing `target_combatant_id` singular. The PRIMARY target (first entry) rides through the existing single-target code path so the legacy response/broadcast fields carry its outcome for backward compat. Each additional target gets its own fresh attack roll + damage roll (RAW: weapon attacks are per-target, not single-roll-spread-N-ways). Per-target outcomes return in a new `auto_attack_targets: list[dict]` array on both the HTTP response and the `weapon_attack` WS broadcast. Auto-uplifts (Hex / Hunter's Mark / Colossus Slayer) intentionally apply only to the primary target — those are target-bound mechanics; spreading their +1d6 across unrelated enemies would be RAW-wrong (filed for follow-up). 4 new harness tests + 31 existing attack tests unchanged. PATCH.
**Description:** Three edits. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::use_attack` — body parsing now extracts `target_combatant_ids` list in addition to the singular. If the list is non-empty, its first entry populates `target_combatant_id` for the existing code path; if only the singular is set, the list becomes `[singular]` for the new code path. Either way the two stay in sync. **(2)** Multi-target loop inserted right after the existing primary-target damage-application block: collects the primary target's outcome (mirroring the legacy fields exactly), then iterates `target_combatant_ids_in[1:]` for additional targets. Per iteration: fresh d20 attack roll using the same to-hit expression (same bonus, same roll_state, same Rage advantage — those are caster + weapon properties, not target properties), fresh damage roll with crit-doubling if applicable, hit determination via `_read_target_ac`, auto-apply if campaign flag is on. Per-target outcome dict captures attack_total + breakdown + is_crit + hit + target_ac + damage_total + breakdown + damage_applied + hp_before/after + resistance/dying/dead flags. **(3)** Broadcast payload + HTTP response both get the new `auto_attack_targets` field; existing fields unchanged. **(4)** `tests/harness/test_attack_multi_target.py` (NEW, 4 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why per-target fresh rolls rather than one roll spread N ways. RAW: D&D 5e weapon attacks are per-target. The Fighter with Extra Attack who swings at two enemies rolls two d20s + two damage dice — not one roll applied to both. Reusing the same attack_total across multiple targets would be RAW-wrong and would mean a high d20 either always hits all targets or always misses all — too binary. Per-target rolls match Magic Missile-style "spread" mechanics ONLY when each missile gets its own roll; SimpleVTT's existing /cast_spell handles that case for spells. /attack is for weapons; fresh rolls are correct.
**Description (cont 2):** Why the primary-target outcome rides the legacy fields. Backward compat. The existing chat-card rendering (in `tabletop.js::renderSpellCast` and friends) reads `attack_total`, `hit`, `damage_applied`, etc. directly from the broadcast. If we'd moved those to live ONLY in `auto_attack_targets[0]`, every single-target attack rendered today would suddenly stop working until the client was updated. The dual-write keeps existing clients happy + lets new clients consume the structured list. Same pattern as `/cast_spell`'s `auto_save_targets` introduction in v2.44.0.
**Description (cont 3):** Why auto-uplifts (Hex / Hunter's Mark / Colossus Slayer) only apply to the primary target. Those mechanics are TARGET-BOUND. Hex is "the marked creature" — a single creature the caster designated. Hunter's Mark is similar. Colossus Slayer fires once per turn on a creature below max HP. None of them have a "applies to all attacks against all targets this turn" semantic in RAW. For multi-target attacks the safe behavior is to apply the uplift only to the target the buff was bound to (the primary one in our model). Per-target uplift detection would require checking each target's buffs vs the attacker's marks — possible but invasive (the v2.20.0 helper assumes a single target). Filed for follow-up.
**Description (cont 4):** Why the multi-target loop uses `attack_id` from the primary attack for damage logging. The `_apply_damage_to_combatant` helper stamps `_attack_damage_log[attack_id]` so the chat card's Undo button can revert damage. With multi-target, all per-target applications share the same `attack_id`. That means Undo currently reverts the LAST applied target's damage only (the log is keyed by attack_id, not (attack_id, target_id)). For v1 of multi-target attacks, "Undo" works for single-target and is best-effort for multi-target. Filed: multi-target Undo with per-target log keys.

Filed: per-target range check for multi-target weapon attacks.

**Description:** Seven edits. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::ruler_broadcast` (NEW endpoint, ~50 lines). POST takes `{action: "show" | "hide", points?: [...], multi_segment?: bool}`. Auth: any campaign member (the ruler is a transient visual cue; no state mutation). 400 for invalid action or non-list points; 403 for non-members. Server side does NO persistence — pure fan-out. **(2)** `app/static/tabletop.js::_rulerPicker` — new `broadcasting: bool` state field; `start({broadcasting})` accepts the flag; `_cleanup` resets it. `addPoint` and `commitMulti` and the single-segment auto-commit each post to the endpoint when broadcasting is true. **(3)** `app/static/tabletop.js::_postRulerBroadcast` (NEW helper) — fire-and-forget POST with the same shape across all three callers. **(4)** `app/static/tabletop.js::_remoteRulers` (NEW Map<user_id, entry>) + `_onRulerBroadcast` handler that the WS dispatcher invokes on `ruler_broadcast` messages. Drops echoes from our own user_id (we already render locally). Sets `expires_at = now + 8000ms` on each show. **(5)** `app/static/tabletop.js::_setRulerButtonState(active, broadcasting)` — updates the button's `aria-pressed` AND `data-broadcasting` attributes; tooltip text adapts to the broadcasting state. **(6)** `app/static/tabletop.js` render pass — new draw block walks `_remoteRulers`, drops expired entries lazily, renders semi-transparent green segments + filled circles + a single chip at the path's midpoint with `${totalFt} ft (${user_name})`. **(7)** `app/templates/tabletop.html` CSS — new `.canvas-tool-btn[data-broadcasting="true"]::after` rule appends a 📡 glyph to the button label. **(8)** `tests/harness/test_ruler_broadcast.py` (NEW, 6 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why the toolbar Shift-click toggles BOTH multi-segment AND broadcast. The GM-led demo use case the plan describes ("show everyone how far my Fire Bolt reaches" / "trace the path the goblin will take") almost always wants the multi-segment + broadcast combination. Two independent toggles would be one click each — three clicks (button + Shift modifier × 2) for the same setup. Binding them at the toolbar level keeps the one-click ergonomic. The endpoint + state flags remain independent so future UX work (e.g. a context menu) can split them.
**Description (cont 2):** Why broadcaster name appears in the chip, not in a sidebar banner. The chip is where the player's attention already is (the line they're being shown). A sidebar / toolbar indicator means looking elsewhere to figure out who's measuring. The chip becomes "X ft (Demo GM)" — context + attribution in one glance. If multiple broadcasters fire at once, each gets their own chip on their own path.
**Description (cont 3):** Why 8 s expiry on the receiving side, not on the broadcasting side. The broadcaster's 3 s ghost (from Phase 1 / 3D) clears the local line + fires a `hide` post. If that POST gets dropped (browser closed, network hiccup, server restart), remote clients would render the ghost forever. The 8 s expiry on receipt = broadcaster's 3 s freeze + 5 s buffer for network jitter — covers the dropped-hide failure mode without dragging out the cleanup beyond what makes sense.
**Description (cont 4):** Why drop our own echoes (`d.user_id === ME.id`). The WS hub fans out to everyone INCLUDING the sender. If we rendered our own echo as a "remote" ruler, it would overlap with the local active picker (we'd see double lines + double chips). Filtering on user_id is the standard hub convention; same pattern as the v2.49.0 concentration AoE update.
**Description (cont 5):** Why server-side does no persistence. The ruler isn't game state — it's a transient communication channel. If a player joins the campaign mid-broadcast, they see the next update (3-second cadence in active mode); they don't need to see history. No DB rows, no in-memory map on the server, no replay logic. Fan-out and done. Mirrors the existing chat-flavor broadcasts (presence, roll) that are likewise fire-and-forget.

Bob tried to Shift-click his own button — broadcasts went out, GM saw "X ft (Bob (Demo Wizard))" overlays. Full regression: 335 harness tests pass (was 329, +6 new). **Commit summary:** **Phase 3D: multi-segment ruler.** Shift+R (or Shift-click on the 📏 Ruler button) starts a multi-segment ruler mode where each click adds a waypoint instead of auto-committing after 2 points. Enter commits + freezes the line for 3 s; Esc cancels. Per-segment chips display each leg's length at its midpoint; a "Σ TOTAL ft" chip floats next to the cursor showing the running total. Existing single-segment behavior is unchanged — Shift toggles between modes. Shared `_drawRulerChip` helper extracted for both segment-midpoint and total chips. No new endpoints; client-only. Plan status: "✅ Phases 1 + 2 + 3A–D shipped · 3E optional." PATCH.
**Description:** Five edits, all in `app/static/tabletop.js`. **(1)** `_rulerPicker` state — new `multiSegment: bool` field defaulting to false. `start(opts)` now accepts `{multiSegment: bool}`. `_cleanup` resets the flag. **(2)** `_rulerPicker.addPoint` — multi-segment branch keeps pushing points without auto-commit; updates the hint banner to show running waypoint count. Single-segment branch is unchanged (2-point auto-commit). **(3)** `_rulerPicker.commitMulti` (NEW) — sums per-segment distances, calls `_showRulerResult(total)`, flips to ghost state for the 3 s freeze. **(4)** Hotkey wiring — `R` starts single-segment (existing); `Shift+R` starts multi-segment; `Enter` / `NumpadEnter` while the multi-segment picker is active with ≥2 points calls `commitMulti()`. Button click also passes `multiSegment: ev.shiftKey` so Shift-click on the toolbar button matches the keyboard. **(5)** Render pass rewritten to walk an "effective path" array (committed points + cursor tail in active mode). Draws dashed segments between consecutive points, filled circles at committed points + an open ring at the cursor preview, per-segment midpoint chips with each leg's distance, and a "Σ TOTAL ft" chip next to the cursor in multi-segment mode with ≥3 effective points (the single-segment chip already shows the only segment's distance, so the summed chip would be redundant). **(6)** Mousemove guard for cursor tracking now matches multi-segment too (cursor follows on any waypoint count when multiSegment is set, vs. only when points.length === 1 in single-segment mode).

The per-segment chips already say "N ft"; a plain "85 ft" at the cursor would be visually identical to a segment chip and a glancing player might think "this segment is 85 ft" when actually the LAST segment is e.g. 15 ft and the total is 85. The Σ glyph (Greek sigma = mathematical "sum") is unambiguous: a player sees Σ → reads as total. The chip's position (offset to upper-right of the cursor, not on the line) further disambiguates it from per-segment chips that sit ON the line.
**Description (cont 2):** Why the 1000-point cap heuristic in `showingCursor`. The condition `_rulerPicker.points.length < (_rulerPicker.multiSegment ? 1000 : 2)` reads as "always show the cursor in multi-segment mode" — 1000 is a generous bound that's effectively unlimited but avoids `Infinity` (which is fine in JS but feels weird in code). **Description (cont 3):** Why no harness tests. Same constraint as every prior ruler / hover / picker commit: HTTP+WS harness can't drive canvas mousedowns or keyboard events. Phase 3D's correctness is verified by clicking around in a browser. Filed: a Playwright spec for the entire ruler family (carries forward from v2.49.71 / .78 / .81 / .82).
**Description (cont 4):** Why Enter and NumpadEnter both. Some users prefer the numpad Enter for spatial reasons (the numpad sits next to the trackpad on many laptops). Listing both `ev.key === 'Enter' || ev.key === 'NumpadEnter'` is a one-line cost for inclusive coverage.

## [2.49.82] - 2026-05-22

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Phase 3C: range ring on cast-button hover.** When the player hovers a 🪄 Cast button in the character sheet's spell list (BEFORE clicking it), a translucent green ring appears around the caster's token on the tabletop at the spell's range — a "where can this reach?" preview. The ring disappears on mouseleave. Cross-window wiring via `postMessage` from the sheet's iframe drawer up to `window.parent` (the tabletop window). Client-side range parser `_parseRangeFtJS` mirrors the v2.49.74 server parser so the sheet sends the raw range string and the tabletop parses on receipt — no client/server version-sync risk. Suppressed when the AoE picker / ruler picker / a drag is active (the more prominent tool wins). Same Phase 3A green-translucent ring primitive. No harness coverage (cross-window postMessage + canvas render — needs Playwright); existing 329 harness tests pass. PATCH.
**Description:** Five edits. **(1)** `app/static/tabletop.js::_parseRangeFtJS` (NEW, ~25 lines) — JS port of the v2.49.74 server-side parser. Same return contract: `null` for unparseable / Special / Unlimited / Sight; `0` for Self / Self+radius (caller skips the ring); `5` for Touch; integer feet for "N feet" / "N ft"; long band for thrown ("20/60 ft" → 60); miles × 5280. **(2)** `app/static/tabletop.js::_castHoverRing` (NEW state + show/hide methods, ~50 lines) — modeled on `_aoePicker`'s shape. `show({char_id, range_str, spell_name})` parses the range, resolves the caster's token position via `_aoePicker._resolveOrigin(charId)`, gates on `range_ft > 0 && !_aoePicker.active && !_rulerPicker.active && !dragging`, sets state, triggers `render()`. `hide()` clears state + re-renders. **(3)** `app/static/tabletop.js` — new `window.addEventListener('message', ...)` listener that dispatches `vtt:cast_range_hover` messages from the sheet to `_castHoverRing.show / .hide`. Origin-matched against `window.location.origin` so a tab in another origin can't spoof the ring. **(4)** `app/static/tabletop.js::render` — new draw pass right before the Phase 3B hover rangefinder. Translucent green ring (alpha 0.06 fill, dashed `#4ade80` 1.5 px stroke) at `(range_ft / 5) * gridSize` radius around the caster's position. **(5)** `app/templates/sheet_dnd5e.html::renderSpells` — new `forEach` loop adding mouseenter / mouseleave handlers to every `.sp-cast` button. Hover posts `{type: 'vtt:cast_range_hover', action: 'show', char_id, range_str, spell_name}` to `window.parent`; leave posts `{action: 'hide'}`. Gated on `window.parent !== window` so the loop is a no-op when the sheet runs standalone (no path back).
**Description (cont):** Why client-side parsing rather than passing a pre-parsed `range_ft` from the sheet. The sheet's spell entries store raw text like `"60 feet"` / `"Self (15-foot cone)"`. Pre-parsing would mean either (a) keeping the sheet aware of every parse rule (duplicates the server logic in a third place), or (b) calling the server to parse before posting (a hot-path AJAX on every hover, bad UX). Pure JS parse on the receiving side: same code path as the server uses, no version-sync risk, no extra HTTP round-trip. The 25-line JS function matches the 100-line Python module in spirit because regexes carry most of the logic.
**Description (cont 2):** Why the GM iframe is the primary supported path. The character sheet opens in either (a) the GM's iframe drawer (`monster-sheet-drawer-iframe` in `tabletop.html`) where `window.parent === tabletop`, or (b) a player's new tab via `<a target="_blank" rel="noopener">` where `window.opener === null` and there's no path back. The Phase 3C ring works in case (a) — which is the primary place the GM hovers a spell button while watching the tabletop. Case (b) silently no-ops (the sheet's `_parentForRing` is null). A future BroadcastChannel-based fan-out could light up case (b) but it's not gating; players who pop the sheet out of the drawer have presumably chosen to detach from the tabletop view.
**Description (cont 3):** Why suppress when AoE picker / ruler picker / drag is active. The hover ring is a passive cue — it shouldn't compete with explicit tool modes. The render-pass guard is the same five-condition set as Phase 3B (drag check via `!dragging`; pickers via `!_aoePicker.active && !_rulerPicker.active`). Phase 3B's hover rangefinder is also active when the user has a target selected; if both fire (player has a target + hovers a spell button), the rangefinder's grey line + chip overlay the green ring — both are subtle so visual conflict is minimal.
**Description (cont 4):** Why origin-matched postMessage. `window.addEventListener('message')` accepts messages from ANY origin by default. A malicious page in another tab could (via `window.open(tabletop_url)` or by being embedded in an iframe somewhere) post `vtt:cast_range_hover` events and spoof the ring on the tabletop. The `ev.origin !== window.location.origin` check rejects those. The sheet posts with `window.location.origin` as the targetOrigin so the browser ALSO rejects cross-origin delivery. Belt + suspenders.
**Description (cont 5):** Why no harness coverage. The behavior depends on (a) cross-window postMessage delivery — the harness's HTTP+WS fixtures don't drive a real browser, and (b) canvas mousemove + render — same Playwright-needed pattern as Phase 1 / 3A client / 3B. Existing 329 tests cover the server-side range-enforcement contract this commit's ring previews; the visual layer is verified by clicking around in a browser. Filed (same Playwright spec follow-up as v2.49.71 / .78 / .81).
**Description (cont 6):** Verification. Manual: opened `/campaign/1` in a browser as GM, opened Thalindra's character sheet in the drawer iframe, hovered the 🪄 Cast button next to Fire Bolt — green ring appeared at 120 ft around Thalindra's token; mouseleave removed it; hover on Magic Missile showed a 120 ft ring; hover on Mage Hand showed a 30 ft ring; hover on Shield (Self) showed nothing (range parses to 0 → suppressed). Container rebuilt to v2.49.82. Full regression: 329 harness tests pass — server / WS contracts unchanged.

### Added
- `app/static/tabletop.js::_parseRangeFtJS` — JS client-side range parser mirroring the server's contract.
- `app/static/tabletop.js::_castHoverRing` — state + show/hide methods for the cast-button hover ring.
- `app/static/tabletop.js` — postMessage listener for `vtt:cast_range_hover`.
- `app/static/tabletop.js::render` — new draw pass for the ring (before the Phase 3B rangefinder pass).
- `app/templates/sheet_dnd5e.html::renderSpells` — mouseenter / mouseleave handlers on `.sp-cast` buttons posting `vtt:cast_range_hover` messages to `window.parent`.

### Changed
- `app/templates/wiki.html` — plan-status row updated.
- `docs/wiki/README.md` — same row update.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure additive. Existing sp-cast click behavior unchanged; the new mouseenter / mouseleave handlers don't interact with the click path.
- **GM-iframe path is the primary supported case.** Player pop-out tabs silently no-op (no path back to the tabletop window).
- **Phase 3C complete.** Remaining: 3D (multi-segment ruler Shift+R), 3E (broadcast mode Shift-click). Both optional per the plan.

### Filed
- **Playwright spec for the ruler / rangefinder family** — covers Phase 1 / 3A / 3B / 3C in one suite. Carried forward.
- **BroadcastChannel-based fan-out for player pop-out tabs** — would light up the hover ring even when the sheet is in a separate tab. Lower priority.
