New file `docs/plans/ruler-and-range.md` covers the requested ruler-button workflow (suspend map control + two left-clicks), evaluates four alternative approaches (drag-mode, hover rangefinder, attached-range overlays, click-drag with modifier), and lays out a three-phase plan: Phase 1 ruler tool client-only, Phase 2 server-side distance helper + spell-range parser + range enforcement with 409 + override on cast/attack endpoints, Phase 3 optional follow-ups (hover rangefinder, range rings, multi-segment, broadcast mode). Includes ASCII mockups of the toolbar insertion, the ruler-active overlay, and the out-of-range cast card. Pulls integration-point file paths + line numbers from a fresh survey of `tabletop.js`, `tabletop_routes.py`, and the spell JSON content layer. NOT IMPLEMENTED — this commit ships only the plan. PATCH — docs-only.
**Description:** One new file. **(1)** `docs/plans/ruler-and-range.md` (NEW). Eight sections: Goal, Constraints surfaced by codebase survey, Approaches considered (A/B/C/D w/ pros/cons), Chosen approach detailed design (client state + mouse integration + rendering + toolbar + hotkeys + visibility broadcast), Range enforcement design (server distance helper + spell-range parser + endpoint integration + 409 shape + when-not-to-enforce + harness tests), Phase 3 follow-ups, Open questions (5 items with recommendations), Implementation phases summary table, File-path index for the implementation agent, Decision log.
**Description (cont):** Why the ruler-button workflow as the primary primitive. The codebase already has an established "suspend map control, prompt for clicks, resume" pattern via the v2.48.0 AoE picker (`tabletop.js:314–527`). The ruler tool is a direct analog — same `start() → Promise → cleanup()` shape, same body-class CSS trick for cursor changes, same Esc/right-click cancel idiom. Two clicks (vs. one drag) gives explicit cancel-after-first-point semantics, and works identically on touch devices where Shift-drag (option B) has no equivalent. Drag-mode is filed for Phase 3 as a power-user shortcut, not the primary UX.
**Description (cont 2):** Why coupling ruler + range enforcement in one plan doc rather than two. They share the same primitive: a "distance between two canvas points" function. The current `token_move` endpoint at `tabletop_routes.py:4929` already has this math (Chebyshev for square, Euclidean for hex, 5 ft / cell). Phase 2 extracts it into `_distance_ft_between_tokens` so both the ruler render AND the cast-endpoint range check use one source of truth. Splitting into two plans would either duplicate the helper design or force a "see the other plan for distance math" cross-reference. Combined plan keeps the rationale in one place.
**Description (cont 3):** Why the plan includes mockups even though markdown can't render real UI images. The "interface changes with mockups" requirement is real — the agent reviewing the plan needs to see the proposed toolbar layout, the ruler overlay, and the out-of-range cast card. ASCII mockups are crude but unambiguous (no rendering dependency), and the file-path index at the end gives the implementation agent exact pixel coordinates (e.g. "insert above the drawer tab bar at `tabletop.html:1216`"). A Figma mockup would be richer but adds an external dependency for what should be a self-contained design doc.
**Description (cont 4):** Decisions captured in the plan (with rationale):
- Picker pattern over drag-mode (discoverability + touch parity).
- Local-only ruler by default; Shift-click broadcasts to all clients (privacy by default).
- Center-to-center distance (matches existing `token_move`; new rules would be a separate decision).
- Range check fires BEFORE slot consumption (mirrors the existing `no_slot` gate ordering).
- One ruler button visible to GM + players (measuring is a player concern, not GM-only).
- `override_range: true` body field for the cast-anyway path (mirrors the existing Phase 4 `override`).
- Spell-range parser as a separate file `app/content/range_parser.py` (isolates content concern from the route file).
**Description (cont 5):** Open questions deliberately surfaced for review:
- 5-5-5 vs. 5-10-5 diagonals (recommend: match token_move = 5-5-5; defer setting unless asked).
- Token edge vs. token center (recommend: center, add edge mode in Phase 3 if asked).
- Cover / line-of-sight (out of scope — separate massive feature).
- Should range-check fire before or after slot consumption (recommend: before; matches existing 409 gate ordering).
- Should the demo seed include a range-demo encounter (recommend: yes, in Phase 2's implementation commit).
**Description (cont 6):** What's NOT covered (filed for follow-up plans):
- Spell line-of-sight (walls / cover).
- Movement-range enforcement (today `token_move` reports distance via WS but doesn't BLOCK; could add per-turn movement budget enforcement).
- Reach-weapon advantage (5 ft melee vs. 10 ft polearm reach gradient).
- Spell save DC = caster's stat-driven DC: orthogonal feature, not range-related.
**Description (cont 7):** Verification. Plan reviewed for consistency with CLAUDE.md harness rule (Phase 2 endpoint commits will ship their own harness tests per the rule; Phase 1 is client-only so no endpoint tests required). Verified against the touch-target rule (44×44 px minimum). Cross-referenced file paths against current code line numbers via codebase survey. Doc-only commit — no functional change; full harness suite unchanged (262 passing).

### Added
- `docs/plans/ruler-and-range.md` — design plan for a ruler tool + server-side range enforcement on cast/attack endpoints. Three implementation phases; recommended approach; alternatives evaluated; ASCII mockups; file-path index for the implementation agent.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Doc-only. No code changes; no API surface change.
- **Connects to several filed items.** Specifically: v2.49.58 Sleep's "20-ft radius enforcement" filed item, v2.49.57 Open Hand Technique's "push_authorized cast-card UI" (the drag-target-15-ft prompt benefits from a range visualization), v2.49.55 Stunning Strike's "must follow a hit" (the melee-hit gate is related to range — both are pre-click validation).
- **No implementation in this commit.** Phases 1 and 2 are separate commits with their own version bumps, code, and harness tests per CLAUDE.md.

### Filed
- **Phase 1 implementation** — ruler tool: `_rulerPicker` + toolbar button + render pass + hotkey. Client-only commit, no endpoint changes. See plan for the exact insertion points.
- **Phase 2 implementation** — `_distance_ft_between_tokens` helper + `app/content/range_parser.py` + range enforcement on `/cast_spell`, `/use_attack`, `/cast_hex`, `/cast_sleep`, `/use_stunning_strike`, `/use_open_hand_technique`. Each endpoint commit ships its own version bump.
- **Phase 3 follow-ups** — hover rangefinder, range rings on cast hover, multi-segment ruler (Shift+R), GM-broadcast mode (Shift-click the button). All optional; ship if user demand surfaces.
- **Movement-range enforcement** — orthogonal to range-on-cast; today `token_move` reports distance via WS but doesn't BLOCK. Future plan; not in this doc.
- **Cover / line-of-sight** — massive separate feature; out of scope for this plan.

## [2.49.58] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Add the Sleep spell — custom HP-pool targeting.** Closes the "Sleep — still absent" filed item from v2.49.55–v2.49.57. RAW (PHB Sleep, 1st-level enchantment, bard/sorcerer/warlock/wizard): roll 5d8 (+2d8 per slot level above 1st) as an HP pool; sort candidate creatures by ascending current HP, ignoring already-unconscious ones; walk the list and put each affected creature to sleep, subtracting their HP from the pool, until the pool is exhausted or there are no candidates left. No save, no concentration. New endpoint `POST /cast_sleep` (dedicated, NOT routed through `/cast_spell` because the HP-pool selector doesn't fit either save-or-suck or save-for-half). The Unconscious key is already in `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS`, so a PC sleeper drops their own concentration via the v2.49.51 hook + emits 💀 — the test pins this end-to-end for the first time on the no-save install path. Also adds Sleep to Thalindra's demo spell list (appended, so existing FIREBALL_INDEX = 7 / Counterspell index assumptions in other harness tests stay intact). 8 new harness tests pin the pool math + ordering invariant + drop-concentration hook + 409 paths. PATCH — additive endpoint + additive seed-list entry; no existing routes or shapes change.
**Description:** Three edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::cast_sleep` (NEW). Body: `{character_id, class_slug, slot_level, target_combatant_ids, override?}`. Validates class (wizard/bard/sorcerer/warlock) + Sleep on the spell list + slot at requested level + Phase 4 action gate (overrideable). Rolls 5d8 + 2d8/level, resolves targets via `_lookup_combatant`, skips already-unconscious + zero-HP, sorts ascending, walks the list installing `unconscious` buffs via `_install_buff` (PC) or `_install_buff_on_combatant_id` (NPC). Marks the action slot + broadcasts a public `roll` event naming the pool + affected list + a `spell_slot_update`. **(2)** `app/demo_seed.py::_wizard_sheet` — appended Sleep to Thalindra's spells. Existing `FIREBALL_INDEX = 7` and Counterspell index references in harness tests are preserved because Sleep lands at index 10 (or 9 in any DB missing Lightning Bolt). **(3)** `tests/harness/test_cast_sleep.py` (NEW, 8 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why a dedicated endpoint rather than routing through `/cast_spell`. Sleep is the only PHB 5e spell with HP-pool targeting; there's no second spell that would amortize a generalized pipeline. `/cast_spell` already branches on save-or-suck vs. save-for-half vs. attack-roll vs. AoE; adding a fifth "HP-pool" branch would tangle the cast-spell handler further. Dedicated endpoint (~280 LOC vs. ~50 LOC of branching in cast_spell, but isolated) follows the cast_hex pattern: Hex also doesn't fit cast_spell's generic shape (unique concentration-buff effects + ability picker).
**Description (cont 2):** Why dice-independent assertions in the ordering test. The pool roll is 5d8 — min 5, max 40, avg 22.5. Asserting a specific affected count would flake. Instead the ordering test asserts the invariants that hold for ANY pool ≥ 5: (a) non-decreasing HP order in `affected`, (b) `sum(affected.hp) <= pool_total`, (c) first `unaffected` (if any) has `hp > pool_remaining` at stop time. Pool=5 → 1+2 affected (3 unaffected); pool=20 → all 3 affected. Both satisfy all three invariants. The "happy path NPC" test uses HP=5 + 5d8 (min=5) for a single-target always-affected case — guaranteed without invariant trickery.
**Description (cont 3):** Why already-unconscious targets are skipped entirely (not "added to unaffected"). RAW: "Creatures within 20 feet of a point you choose within range are affected in ascending order of their current hit points (**ignoring unconscious creatures**)." Skipped from the ordering AND the response — the spell doesn't waste pool on already-asleep creatures, and the response shouldn't report them as "not affected" (which would imply they were considered). The test asserts the already-unconscious bandit appears in neither `affected` nor `unaffected` — clear semantics for the cast-card UI.
**Description (cont 4):** Why this pins the v2.49.51 hook for the third time, and what's new about this branch. v2.49.51 covers the hook generically. The two prior end-to-end tests pin it for: (a) Hold Person (concentration=True, save-or-suck via /cast_spell PC roll_request), (b) Stunning Strike (concentration=False, save-or-suck via /use_stunning_strike PC roll_request). Sleep is the **first no-save** path: the install isn't gated on a saving throw; Thalindra picks the targets and they sleep based on pool math. The hook fires the same way (key="unconscious" matches `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS`), but exercised through the no-save call site rather than the save-or-suck pipeline. Reaffirms that the hook is install-site-agnostic.
**Description (cont 5):** Why Thalindra's seed list adds Sleep at the END. Existing harness tests reference `FIREBALL_INDEX = 7` and other hardcoded spell positions. Inserting Sleep at index 3 (next to Magic Missile, alphabetical-by-level) would shift Fireball to index 8 and break every cast-spell-aoe test. Appending keeps every existing index stable.
**Description (cont 6):** What's NOT modelled here. **Undead / immune-to-charm exclusion** — RAW excludes undead + creatures immune to charm. SimpleVTT doesn't track creature-type immunities consistently, so v1 trusts the GM to deselect inappropriate targets via the candidate-list input. **Wake-on-damage** — RAW: "the sleeper takes damage [...] [wakes them] awake." The existing damage pipeline doesn't auto-clear the Unconscious buff on damage; the GM runs `/end_buff unconscious` manually. **Wake-via-shake** — no `/shake_awake` endpoint; `/end_buff unconscious` covers it for now. **20-ft radius enforcement** — no spatial range yet; the candidate list IS the radius from the GM's perspective (filed as coupled to the ruler/range work being planned separately).
**Description (cont 7):** Verification. Ran the new tests pre-fix: all 8 failed with 404 (endpoint missing) + 409 spell_not_known (Sleep not on Thalindra's list). Post-fix: all 8 pass. Full regression: 262 harness tests pass total (was 254, +8 new) — one pre-existing flaky attack-crit test occasionally trips; not my doing and not load-bearing. 33 encounter-sim tests unchanged.

### Added
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::cast_sleep` — new endpoint `POST /api/campaign/{cid}/cast_sleep`. Validates class + Sleep on list + slot + Phase 4 gate; rolls 5d8 + 2d8/level pool; sorts targets by ascending current HP, skips already-unconscious; walks the list installing Unconscious via `_install_buff` (PC) / `_install_buff_on_combatant_id` (NPC).
- `app/demo_seed.py::_wizard_sheet` — Sleep appended to Thalindra's spell list (`_slug: "sleep"`, level 1, prepared, 1 action). Appended to preserve existing harness spell-index references.
- `tests/harness/test_cast_sleep.py` — 8 tests (happy path NPC / ordering invariant / high HP skip / already-unconscious skip / drops PC concentration / upcast scales pool / no_slot / wrong_class).
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry; total 254 → 262.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure additive: new endpoint, new seed-list entry appended at the end. Existing `/cast_spell` behavior + every other endpoint unchanged. Existing harness `FIREBALL_INDEX = 7` / Counterspell index assumptions preserved by appending Sleep.
- **Third install-site for the v2.49.51 hook.** First was Hold Person (concentration=True save-or-suck PC), second was Stunning Strike (concentration=False save-or-suck PC), third is Sleep (no-save, no concentration, install-by-pool-math). Same hook fires; same 💀 log emits; install-site-agnostic.
- **Dice path uses the seeded RNG.** `dice_mod.roll("5d8")` honors the `DICE_SEED` env var so seeded test runs would be deterministic. The harness tests assert dice-independent invariants anyway — no DICE_SEED needed.

### Filed
- **Undead / immune-to-charm exclusion** — needs creature-type tagging on monster templates to enforce automatically. v1 trusts the GM to deselect inappropriate targets.
- **Wake-on-damage** — when a sleeper takes damage, RAW wakes them. The damage pipeline could check for `unconscious` source=`Sleep` and call `_remove_buff` after applying damage. Out of scope here.
- **Wake-via-shake** — `/shake_awake` endpoint that takes another creature's action to wake a sleeping ally. Or just `/end_buff unconscious` for now.
- **20-ft radius enforcement** — coupled to the ruler/range planning work. Currently the candidate list IS the radius.
- **Bard / Sorcerer / Warlock spell lists** — Sleep is RAW on all four lists but only Thalindra's demo seed has it. Add to Lyra (Bard), Zara (Sorcerer), Magnus (Warlock) so all eligible classes can demo the spell. Trivial follow-up.
- **Open Hand Technique PC tests** — carried forward from v2.49.57.

## [2.49.57] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Add Monk Open Hand Technique (Way of the Open Hand, Lv 3+ subclass feature).** Closes the "Open Hand Technique" filed item from v2.49.55. RAW: when monk hits with a Flurry of Blows attack, they may impose one of three riders — Prone (DEX save), Push 15 ft (STR save), or No Reactions (no save, 1 turn). No additional ki cost (the Flurry already paid). New endpoint `POST /use_open_hand_technique` takes a `mode` param (`prone` | `push` | `no_reactions`). Prone routes through the save-or-suck pipeline using a new `open-hand-prone` entry in `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP`. Push uses the same pipeline structurally but has NO map entry — the response carries `push_authorized` so the GM UI can drag the token; no buff installs. No Reactions skips the save entirely and installs a `reaction-denied` buff inline (`concentration: False`, `duration_rounds: 1`) plus a public roll-log entry. 5 new harness tests pin all three modes + 409 wrong_class + 400 bad_mode. PATCH — additive endpoint; existing routes and broadcast shapes unchanged.
**Description:** Three edits. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP` — added `"open-hand-prone"` entry. `key: "prone"`, `concentration: False`, `duration_rounds: 10` (Prone has no RAW timer — ends when the prone creature spends half movement to stand; 10 rounds is a generous default and the GM ends it via `/end_buff`). Effects list summarizes the RAW prone-condition rider. Crucially **not** in `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS` — Prone constrains movement / grants advantage at melee + disadvantage at range, but doesn't incapacitate. **(2)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::use_open_hand_technique` — new `POST /api/campaign/{cid}/use_open_hand_technique` endpoint. Validates monk + Way of the Open Hand + Lv 3+. Branches on `mode`: no_reactions is the early-return inline-install path (mirrors `/use_rage` / `/use_bardic_inspiration` "install + announce"); prone + push share the save pipeline (same DC math + roll_request setup as Stunning Strike). **(3)** `tests/harness/test_use_open_hand_technique.py` (NEW, 5 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why one endpoint with a `mode` param rather than three separate endpoints. RAW the three options are one feature with one "choose at use time" gate. Splitting into `/use_open_hand_prone` / `/use_open_hand_push` / `/use_open_hand_no_reactions` would triple the validation boilerplate (monk + subclass + level + target lookup all repeat) and force three almost-identical chat-card buttons. A single endpoint with a discriminator keeps the validation in one place + matches how the future UI surfaces the feature (one button with a popover that picks the mode). The mode whitelist (`prone` / `push` / `no_reactions`) is the same shape as `class_slug` parameters on existing multi-class spell-cast endpoints.
**Description (cont 2):** Why push has no `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP` entry. Push doesn't install a buff — it grants the monk permission to physically move the target up to 15 ft. SimpleVTT today doesn't enforce movement, so the push is a GM-facing "drag the token" instruction. The response carries `push_authorized: True` (on save fail) / `False` (on pass) so the cast-card UI can render a "Drag target up to 15 ft from monk" prompt. For PC targets the save is rolled by the player via roll_request; the GM observes the save total in the roll log and acts (the /respond handler's install branch is a no-op because `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP.get("open-hand-push")` is None). For NPC targets the server rolls inline and `push_authorized` ships in the same response.
**Description (cont 3):** Why no_reactions skips the save pipeline entirely. RAW has no save — the rider just lands. Routing through the save-or-suck pipeline would mean creating a sham DC=0 roll_request with no decision branches; cleaner to install inline + broadcast a public roll-log entry. Mirrors the no-save inline-install path in `/use_rage` (rage buff lands without a roll) and `/use_bardic_inspiration` (inspiration die buff lands without a roll). The `reaction-denied` buff key is custom (not a standard 5e condition) — `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP` doesn't help here because there's no roll outcome to gate on; the buff dict is constructed inline.
**Description (cont 4):** Subclass validation. Sheet stores `"subclass": "Way of the Open Hand"`. Endpoint normalizes via `(sheet.get("subclass") or "").lower()` and checks `"open hand" in subclass`. Substring-match keeps the gate forgiving for cosmetic variations ("Way of The Open Hand", "Open Hand Tradition", etc.) while still rejecting other monk subclasses ("Way of Shadow", "Way of the Four Elements"). 409 `wrong_subclass` with `expected: "way of the open hand"` and `got: <whatever the sheet says>` so the UI can render a helpful error.
**Description (cont 5):** Test strategy. NPC happy paths (prone + push) use the same retry-loop pattern as the Stunning Strike NPC happy path because the save is random. The push test asserts the inverse-correlation invariant (`push_authorized == not auto_save_passed`) which is a single-iteration check — push is interesting in both branches. No_reactions is deterministic (no roll) — single-call assert. wrong_class + bad_mode are deterministic error-paths.
**Description (cont 6):** Verification. Ran the new tests pre-fix: all 5 failed with 404. Post-fix: all 5 pass. Full regression: 254 harness tests pass (was 249, +5 new); 33 encounter-sim tests still pass.

### Added
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP["open-hand-prone"]` — new entry with `key: "prone"`, `concentration: False`, `duration_rounds: 10`. NOT in `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS` (Prone doesn't incapacitate RAW).
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::use_open_hand_technique` — new endpoint `POST /api/campaign/{cid}/use_open_hand_technique`. Validates monk + Way of the Open Hand + Lv 3+. Modes: `prone`, `push`, `no_reactions`.
- `tests/harness/test_use_open_hand_technique.py` — 5 tests (prone NPC / push NPC / no_reactions NPC / wrong_class / bad_mode).
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry; total 249 → 254.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure additive. New endpoint + new map entry; no existing routes or shapes change.
- **PC roll_request paths.** Prone PC routes through the same `_save_request_context` + `/respond` install pipeline as Stunning Strike PC (already pinned by `test_stunning_strike_pc_drops_own_concentration`). Push PC stashes a context with `spell_slug: "open-hand-push"` which has no map entry — `/respond`'s install branch is a no-op by design. End-to-end PC tests for Open Hand are filed below.
- **No "must follow Flurry hit" enforcement.** Same trust-the-caller convention as Stunning Strike. UI is expected to gate the button on the most-recent Flurry hit outcome.

### Filed
- **PC integration tests for Open Hand** — happy-path PC for each of the three modes. Prone PC mirrors Stunning Strike's PC test (now pinned). Push PC needs a new assertion shape (the /respond handler doesn't install a buff but the GM should still see the save total in the roll log). No-reactions PC mirrors the no-save NPC test with a PC target. All three are similar enough that one combined PC test could cover the file.
- **`push_authorized` cast-card UI** — when push mode resolves with `push_authorized: True`, the cast card should render a "Drag target up to 15 ft from monk" affordance and ideally a range-aware drag preview. Coupled to the ruler/range work being planned separately.
- **Wholeness of Body, Tranquility, Quivering Palm** — the remaining Way of the Open Hand features (Lv 6 / 11 / 17). All present in the SRD JSON but not yet endpointed. Lower priority than core class features at typical play levels.
- **Sleep** — still absent. Custom HP-pool targeting; next up.

NPC targets get a server-rolled save inline. PC targets get a roll_request the player owner /responds to (same path as Hold Person). 3 new harness tests pin happy-path NPC + wrong_class + no_ki. **Description:** Three edits. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP` — added a new `"stunning-strike"` entry with `key: "stunned"`, `concentration: False`, `duration_rounds: 1`, RAW effects list. Body: `{character_id, target_combatant_id?, target_character_id?, target_name?}`. Validates monk class + level >= 5 + ki >= 1, then spends 1 ki, computes save DC = 8 + monk prof + monk WIS mod, and routes through either the NPC server-rolled save path (mirrors cast_spell line ~7440) or the PC roll_request path (mirrors line ~7392). On fail the existing save-or-suck install code at line ~6564 picks up the slug from `_save_request_context` and installs Stunned via `_install_buff` (PC) / `_install_buff_on_combatant_id` (NPC inline above). Stunning Strike is a free interrupt RAW, so no action / bonus / reaction slot is consumed (only ki). **(3)** `tests/harness/test_use_stunning_strike.py` (NEW, 3 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why route through `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP` rather than write a bespoke install. The save-or-suck pipeline already handles three coupled concerns: (a) the DC computation + save-roll broadcast + result correlation back to the cast card, (b) the buff dict construction with correct source/duration/concentration/effects, (c) the v2.49.51 incapacitation hook firing via `_install_buff`. Reusing the pipeline keeps Stunning Strike consistent with Hold Person etc.: a future GM-facing "save events" filter will surface stuns the same way it surfaces hold-persons. Cost: a slug naming convention that conflates "spell" and "class feature." Acceptable trade.
**Description (cont 2):** Why Stunning Strike is the right first non-concentration incapacitating impl. Alternatives considered: **Sleep** — 1d8-per-slot HP pool affects creatures by ascending HP, no save, unique selection mechanic that doesn't fit any existing endpoint pattern; would need a custom targeting flow (~3× the LOC). **Power Word Stun** — 150-HP threshold then 1-CHA-save mechanic, narrower use case, requires high-level seed setup. **Banishment** — RAW debatable on incapacitation; impl in SimpleVTT today is removal-from-init (different code path entirely). It's an interrupt that piggybacks on an attack, not an action of its own. The attack itself consumes the action; Stunning Strike is the rider. The endpoint enforces ki consumption but skips action / bonus / reaction marking. (Compare /use_lay_on_hands which marks the action slot — Lay on Hands IS the paladin's action, RAW.) The "must follow a hit" constraint is filed for the client-side UI (the chat-card "Stun?" button should only appear after a successful melee hit); the endpoint itself trusts the caller, matching the override-friendly convention of other class-feature endpoints.

The 409 paths are deterministic (no dice) — single-call assertions.

## [2.49.54] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Fix RAW bug: swap loop wrongly dropped paired conditions from other casters.** Closes the bug filed in v2.49.53. PHB p.203 RAW: "you can only concentrate on ONE spell at a time" applies per-caster. A paired condition buff on a victim — e.g. Paralyzed on a Hold Person victim, where `source_char_id` is the enemy caster — is sustained by the SOURCE caster's concentration, not the victim's. The victim casting a new concentration spell of their own should NOT drop the paired condition (otherwise a Held victim could "shake off" being Held by casting Hex, which is wrong RAW + bad gameplay). Pre-fix, `_install_buff`'s swap loop dropped every `concentration: True` buff on the combatant when a new concentration buff landed, regardless of who sourced the existing ones. v2.49.53 already added the source filter to the 🔁 log emission (so the audit was correct); v2.49.54 applies the same filter to the underlying BEHAVIOR so the buff is preserved, not just the log. The fix is a 5-line addition inside the swap loop: when `b.get("source_char_id")` is non-null and != self, append the buff to `new_list` instead of marking it as replaced. 2 new harness tests pin the new behavior + a regression guard for legitimate own-anchor swaps. PATCH — bug fix; no schema or API contract change.
**Description:** Two edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_install_buff` swap loop — inside the `if is_concentration and b.get("concentration"):` branch, added a new check before marking the buff as replaced: if `b.get("source_char_id")` is non-null AND != `character_id`, append the buff to `new_list` (preserve it) and `continue` instead of falling through to the replace path. This filter mirrors the one already applied to (a) `_drop_caster_concentration` (v2.49.51) and (b) the v2.49.53 🔁 log emission — three places now share the same "is this buff actually owned by this combatant?" predicate. **(2)** `tests/harness/test_swap_preserves_paired_buffs.py` (NEW, 2 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why the fix landed via the swap loop rather than upstream. The bug class is: "concentration-flagged buffs on a combatant might be owned by them OR by someone else." Every code path that iterates `target.get("buffs")` and treats `concentration: True` as "this combatant's anchor" has the same bug latent in it. v2.49.51 fixed `_drop_caster_concentration`. v2.49.53 fixed the 🔁 log. v2.49.54 fixes the swap loop. The remaining sites: `_concentration_buff_for` (used by `_maybe_concentration_save`) — also has the bug latent but a paired-condition victim taking damage and rolling a "CON save" for someone else's concentration spell is an edge case worth filing separately. Tracked in the Filed section below.
**Description (cont 2):** Why a victim shouldn't be able to "drop" the paired condition by casting their own concentration spell. The Hold Person caster is the one sustaining the spell via their own concentration; what happens to THE VICTIM's concentration doesn't end the source caster's spell. The victim can't unilaterally end someone else's spell by casting their own — only the source caster's actions (damage taken → failed CON save, voluntary end, incapacitation, death) end Hold Person. If the victim could end the paired buff by casting their own concentration spell, that'd be a major gameplay break.
**Description (cont 3):** Why a regression guard for own-anchor swap. The source filter narrows the swap-loop drop condition. The risk in narrowing is over-narrowing: if the filter accidentally protected own anchors too, casting a new concentration spell wouldn't replace the old one — broken RAW one-at-a-time. The regression test pre-seeds Magnus with `concentration-bless` (source=Magnus), casts Hex, and asserts the anchor was DROPPED. Without this test, an over-broad filter (e.g. `if b.get("source_char_id") is not None` without the `!= self` clause) would silently regress all swaps.
**Description (cont 4):** Why this isn't catching a real incident yet. The current demo doesn't have a flow that triggers the bug naturally — to be a Hold Person victim AND cast a new concentration spell, the victim has to first be paralyzed (which incapacitates them, blocking spell casting). Sleep / Suggestion / Calm Emotions are non-incapacitating concentration spells that leave the victim able to cast — but those aren't in the demo. The bug was discovered while writing v2.49.53's harness test setup (which deliberately constructs a paired-buff scenario via `/battle` PUT to bypass the can't-cast-while-paralyzed gate). Filing the fix now keeps the rule semantically correct ahead of future spell additions.
**Description (cont 5):** Verification. Ran `test_paired_buff_preserved_when_caster_swaps` pre-fix: failed (Paralyzed dropped from Magnus's buff list after Hex install). Post-fix: passes (both buffs co-exist). `test_own_anchor_swap_still_works` passed both before and after — the regression guard. Full regression: 245 harness tests pass (was 243, +2 new); 33 encounter-sim tests still pass. No existing tests touched the bug condition so no surprise breakages.

### Fixed
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_install_buff` swap loop — applies the `source_char_id is None or == character_id` filter inside the swap branch. Paired condition buffs from other casters are now preserved when the combatant casts a new concentration spell. Matches the source filter already applied in `_drop_caster_concentration` (v2.49.51) and the 🔁 log emission (v2.49.53).

### Added
- `tests/harness/test_swap_preserves_paired_buffs.py` — 2 tests (paired-buff-preserved / own-anchor-still-replaces).
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry; total 243 → 245.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure behavior fix — no schema, broadcast shape, or response shape change. Existing callers and tests are unaffected (none triggered the bug condition because the demo lacks non-incapacitating concentration-spell-on-victim flows). The fix is forward-compatible with Sleep, Suggestion, Calm Emotions, etc.
- **Source-filter is now the canonical predicate**: `source_char_id is None or == character_id` means "this combatant is concentrating on this buff." Three call sites now use it: `_drop_caster_concentration` (v2.49.51), `_install_buff` 🔁 log (v2.49.53), `_install_buff` swap loop (this commit). If a fourth site emerges, refactor into a helper.

### Filed
- **`_concentration_buff_for` has the same latent bug** — it returns the first `concentration: True` buff on a combatant without checking source. Used by `_maybe_concentration_save` (the CON-save-on-damage path). A paired-condition victim taking damage would roll a save against the DC for their suffered buff, treating it as their own concentration. Out of scope here; filed for a separate audit.
- **Helper-ify the source-filter predicate** — three call sites use the same `src is None or src == character_id` pattern. A `_is_own_concentration_buff(buff, character_id) -> bool` helper would dedupe. Punt unless a fourth site lands.

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **🔁 GM audit log when a caster swaps to a new concentration spell.** Closes the swap-replaced-by-new-cast follow-up filed in v2.49.52. Pre-fix, `_install_buff` silently dropped the old concentration anchor via the RAW one-at-a-time rule — the `buff_update` broadcast carried `replaced_concentration` keys but no narrative roll-log entry. Fix captures the (key, name, source_char_id) of each replaced concentration buff DURING the swap loop, then after the existing broadcast + paired-cleanup + 💀 paths run, emits a `type=roll` GM-only entry for each replaced anchor: `note=f"🔁 NAME swapped concentration: OLD → NEW"` and breakdown `f"Concentration swapped — cast NEW"`. PATCH — additive log; broadcast shape and `/cast_*` response shape unchanged.
**Description:** Two edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_install_buff` — added a parallel list `replaced_concentration_meta: list[tuple[str, str, object]]` capturing `(key, name, source_char_id)` for each buff dropped by the existing swap loop. After the v2.49.51 💀 emission block (so the 💀 takes precedence on the incapacitation path), emit a `type=roll` GM-only event per replaced anchor when `is_concentration AND replaced_concentration_meta AND not incapacitates_target`, filtered to entries where `old_src is None or old_src == character_id`. **(2)** `tests/harness/test_swap_concentration_log.py` (NEW, 3 tests). Test strategy uses `/battle` PUT to pre-seed a concentration buff on the caster's combatant — the demo doesn't expose two different concentration-spell endpoints for any single PC (Hex is Warlock-only, Hunter's Mark is Ranger-only, save-or-suck concentration spells aren't all on one spell list), so seeding is the cleanest way to exercise the swap path with a known-different key.
**Description (cont):** Why filter by `source_char_id` on the REPLACED buffs. The swap loop's pre-v2.49.53 behavior — `if is_concentration and b.get("concentration"): replaced_concentration_keys.append(b_key); continue` — looks at the concentration flag without checking who's actually concentrating. If Magnus is a Hold Person victim (carrying Paralyzed flagged `concentration: True` with `source_char_id` = enemy caster) AND Magnus casts Hex, the swap loop wrongly treats Paralyzed as Magnus's anchor and drops it. That's a separate bug (filed below). The 🔁 log's source filter prevents the bug from producing misleading audit entries — even though the buff was dropped, Magnus wasn't actually concentrating on it, so "Magnus swapped concentration: Paralyzed → Hex" would be wrong narrative.
**Description (cont 2):** Why `not incapacitates_target` is the right guard rather than `not replaced_concentration_keys.intersection(preexisting_own_anchors)`. When Tavik Hold-Persons Magnus, the RAW cause is incapacitation — the v2.49.51 path emits 💀 for Magnus's lost Hex. The swap loop ALSO drops Hex (because Paralyzed is `concentration: True`). Pre-v2.49.53 these were silent; with both paths emitting logs, we'd get DOUBLE entries: one 💀 ("Magnus lost concentration on Hex — incapacitated (Paralyzed)") plus one 🔁 ("Magnus swapped concentration: Hex → Paralyzed"). The 💀 names the actual RAW reason; the 🔁 names a mechanical side-effect. Skipping 🔁 when `incapacitates_target` is True keeps the log cleaner — one event, one log entry.
**Description (cont 3):** Test approach: `/battle` PUT pre-seeding. The seed inserts a buff dict directly into Magnus's combatant `buffs` array; subsequent `/cast_hex` runs `_install_buff` which sees the seeded buff in `target.get("buffs")` and processes it through the swap loop. This bypasses the spell-casting validation (slot consumption, class check, etc.) for the seeded buff while still exercising the install path under test. Three scenarios:
  1. Own-anchor swap (positive): seeded buff has `source_char_id` = Magnus → 🔁 fires, log names "concentration-bless → Hex."
  2. Paired-buff swap (negative): seeded buff has `source_char_id` = 99999 (an enemy marker) → swap loop still drops it (bug) but 🔁 log does NOT fire — that's the source filter doing its job.
  3. Fresh install (negative): no seeded buff → swap loop has nothing to replace; no 🔁 log.
**Description (cont 4):** Verification. Ran the new tests pre-fix: all 3 failed (no 🔁 broadcast). Post-fix: all 3 pass. Full regression: 243 harness tests pass (was 240, +3 new); 33 encounter-sim tests still pass.

- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry; total 240 → 243.

### Notes

## [2.49.51] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **RAW: incapacitating a concentrating PC now drops THEIR concentration, with a 💀 GM log naming the cause.** Closes the non-damage incapacitation gap filed in v2.49.49. PHB p.203: "you also lose concentration on a spell if you are incapacitated or killed." Pre-fix, when an enemy caster Hold-Personed a Hex'd PC, the visible OUTCOME was correct (Hex dropped) — but only because the existing concentration-swap logic in `_install_buff` accidentally produced it: Paralyzed has `concentration: True`, so it "replaced" Hex via the one-concentration-at-a-time rule. The cause was wrong (the PC isn't choosing to concentrate on Paralyzed; they're suffering it) and there was no audit log to explain the drop. Fix makes the incapacitation drop explicit + load-bearing: a new `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS` frozenset enumerates the RAW-incapacitating condition keys (paralyzed / incapacitated / stunned / petrified / unconscious / asleep). When `_install_buff` lands one of these on a target, it snapshots the target's OWN concentration anchors BEFORE the replacement loop, lets the existing replacement run, then emits a 💀 GM-only log per anchor naming the incapacitating buff. If the incapacitating buff itself is `concentration: False` (e.g. future Sleep impl), the anchor is also explicitly removed via `_remove_buff` so the fix isn't dependent on the swap-by-concentration heuristic. `_drop_caster_concentration` is refined to filter by `source_char_id` so paired condition buffs from other casters aren't swept when the helper fires (death-save callers also benefit — dead PC drops only their own anchors, not paired conditions another caster is concentrating on them with). 3 new harness tests pin the new behavior + a regression guard for the v2.38.0 paired-cleanup path. PATCH — bug fix + log addition; reuses existing broadcast shapes.
**Description:** Three edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py` — new `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS = frozenset({"paralyzed", "incapacitated", "stunned", "petrified", "unconscious", "asleep"})` constant near `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP`. Charmed and Frightened deliberately excluded — those conditions constrain action choice but don't incapacitate per RAW. **(2)** `_install_buff` — before the existing replacement loop, computes `incapacitates_target = key in _INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS and (src_of_new is None or src_of_new != character_id)` (the second clause skips the bizarre self-cast-Hideous-Laughter edge case), then snapshots `preexisting_own_anchors` (concentration-flagged buffs where `source_char_id` is None or == character_id — i.e. anchors the target is concentrating on, not paired conditions from other casters). After the existing replacement + paired-cleanup runs, if `incapacitates_target` AND `preexisting_own_anchors` is non-empty: for each anchor, (a) if it's still in `new_list` (incapacitating buff wasn't concentration=True so the swap didn't remove it), call `_remove_buff` to drop it cleanly; (b) emit a `type=roll` GM-only log with note `f"💀 {caster_name} lost concentration on {anchor_name}"` and breakdown `f"Concentration ends — incapacitated ({buff_label})"`. **(3)** `_drop_caster_concentration` — added `source_char_id` filter (`src is not None and src != character_id` → skip). Necessary so the helper doesn't sweep paired conditions when called by a death-save handler on a victim of someone else's Hold Person. **(4)** `tests/harness/test_incapacitation_drops_concentration.py` (NEW, 3 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why the fix works through `_install_buff` rather than a higher-level hook in `cast_spell`. `_install_buff` is the chokepoint every PC-targeting buff install routes through (PC-failed-save resolution at line 6564, direct PC buff installs at lines 10090/10434/10672, etc.). Hooking here means a future Sleep / Stunning Strike / Power Word Stun endpoint that lands an incapacitating condition gets the RAW drop for free. The NPC path (`_install_buff_on_combatant_id`, line 512) is NOT hooked because NPCs don't track their own concentration anchors in our current implementation — adding the helper there is filed for the NPC-concentration follow-up if/when that lands.
**Description (cont 2):** Why both the "existing replacement already handles it" AND the new hook need to coexist. The existing replacement (line 411: `if is_concentration and b.get("concentration")`) drops Hex when Paralyzed lands because BOTH are flagged concentration. This is right outcome / wrong cause: the swap rule treats the victim as "switching" concentration spells, when RAW says they're losing it because they're incapacitated. Three reasons to add the explicit hook even though the visible outcome currently matches:
  1. **Log emission**. The swap path emits no GM log; the player sees the buff disappear but the GM has no audit entry. The new 💀 log names the cause.
  2. **Non-concentration incapacitation**. The day someone adds Sleep (RAW: target falls Unconscious, NOT a concentration spell), the swap rule wouldn't fire (different flags). The explicit `_remove_buff` call covers it.
  3. **Semantic correctness**. The reason field in the log carries "incapacitated (Paralyzed)" not "concentration swap." A future telemetry consumer can filter on the right cause.
**Description (cont 3):** Why `_drop_caster_concentration` needed the source filter. Before the v2.49.51 change, the helper scanned every `concentration: True` buff on the target combatant. If a PC was a victim of someone else's Hold Person (carrying a Paralyzed buff with source_char_id=enemy), AND the PC also had a concentration anchor of their own (e.g. they were Hexing someone before getting paralyzed), AND the PC died — the death-save handler called `_drop_caster_concentration` which would have scanned the victim's buff list and tried to drop BOTH their Hex anchor AND the Paralyzed buff sourced by the other caster. Dropping Paralyzed from the victim is wrong: the source caster is still concentrating on it; the paralyzed-on-victim should only drop when the source caster's concentration ends. The new filter `src is None or src == character_id` keeps the helper scoped to anchors the target owns. Existing callers (roll_death_save, override_death_save) keep working because anchors have source_char_id=None (Hex) or src=self (concentration-spell-slug anchor from save-or-suck PC-fail path).
**Description (cont 4):** Test design. `test_paralyzed_pc_drops_own_concentration` is the load-bearing test: Magnus has Hex, Tavik Hold-Persons Magnus, Magnus fails save → asserts Paralyzed landed, Hex gone, AND the 💀 GM log fired with "Paralyzed" in the breakdown. Retry loop because the save outcome is random; 15 retries gives ~99.99% chance of one failure given Magnus's low WIS save. `test_charmed_pc_keeps_own_concentration` is the negative-control: Charmed lands → Hex stays (only incapacitating keys trigger the drop). Gracefully no-ops if the seeded spell index doesn't expose Charm Person. `test_source_caster_concentration_still_cascades` guards against the source-filter regressing the v2.38.0 paired-cleanup: Tavik Hold-Persons Magnus, then Tavik manually ends his own concentration → Magnus's Paralyzed should still drop via the existing cascade.
**Description (cont 5):** Verification. Ran `test_paralyzed_pc_drops_own_concentration` pre-fix (just the filter, no explicit log emission): test passed on the visible state (Hex dropped via swap) but the 💀 log assertion failed (no log emitted). Post-fix: all 3 pass. Full regression: 237 harness tests pass (was 234, +3 new); 33 encounter-sim tests still pass. Also caught a pre-existing flake in `test_roll_3_failures_emits_skull_log` (v2.49.50) — the test exhausted Magnus's Warlock slots when the loop ran 15 iterations in a suite-order context that had used Magnus earlier; added a `long_rest` inside the retry loop. That's an unrelated robustness fix bundled in this commit because it surfaced during regression validation; ordinarily it'd be its own bump, but the fix is one line and bundling avoids a no-op v2.49.50.1.

### Fixed
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_install_buff` — when an incapacitating buff lands on a target, the target's OWN concentration anchors drop (regardless of whether the incoming buff is concentration=True or False) and a 💀 GM log entry emits naming the incapacitating buff as the cause.
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_drop_caster_concentration` — filters by `source_char_id` so paired condition buffs from other casters aren't swept when the helper fires for the target's own death.
- `tests/harness/test_concentration_skull_log.py::test_roll_3_failures_emits_skull_log` — long-rests Magnus inside the retry loop to avoid suite-order slot exhaustion. (Pre-existing v2.49.50 flake surfaced during v2.49.51 regression validation.)

### Added
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS` — frozenset of RAW-incapacitating condition keys.
- `tests/harness/test_incapacitation_drops_concentration.py` — 3 tests (paralyzed-drops-hex / charmed-keeps-hex / paired-cleanup-cascade-regression).
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry; total 234 → 237.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Broadcast shape unchanged; the 💀 log uses the same `type=roll` + `visibility=gm_only` envelope as v2.49.50.
- **NPC path not hooked.** `_install_buff_on_combatant_id` (line 512) handles NPC targets and is unchanged. NPCs don't track their own concentration anchors in the current implementation; if NPC-concentration lands as a feature, that helper can mirror the v2.49.51 pattern.

### Filed
- **Sleep / Stunning Strike / Power Word Stun endpoints** — currently absent from the demo. When added, the buff keys ("unconscious" / "stunned") are already in `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS` so the drop fires for free, but the spell impls themselves need to land.
- **Banishment** — RAW banished creatures are incapacitated per most readings. SimpleVTT's banishment impl (if any) removes the combatant from init rather than installing a condition buff; if a "banished" buff key is added, include it in `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS`.
- **NPC concentration** — if NPCs ever sustain concentration spells in our system, `_install_buff_on_combatant_id` needs the same hook.

## [2.49.50] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Distinguish 💀 incapacitation drops from 💔 failed-save drops in the GM concentration log.** Closes the UI-tag follow-up filed in v2.49.48. Pre-fix, every concentration drop emitted the same `💔 NAME lost concentration on SPELL` log — failed CON save, 0-HP forced drop, death-save → dead, GM override → dead all looked identical to the GM. The 0-HP case was the most misleading: the save was still rolled (may have been a nat-20), but the log claimed it "failed." Fix splits the emoji + breakdown: 💔 = failed CON save (existing path), 💀 = incapacitated (0 HP or death-save-state transition). The broadcast shape is unchanged (still `type=roll` with `visibility=gm_only`); the cause distinction is in the note text + breakdown so existing handlers that filter on type+visibility continue to work. Reason strings carry the source: "incapacitated (0 HP)", "3 failed death saves", "GM override → {dying|stable|dead}". 4 new harness tests pin all four log shapes. PATCH — log text change; no schema or API contract change.
**Description:** Two file edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_drop_caster_concentration` — accepts a new keyword-only ``reason: str = "incapacitated"`` param. Before calling `_remove_buff`, snapshots each concentration buff's key + name + paired-buff list (the cleanup helper mutates state in place, so reading after-the-fact returns empty paired lists). After successful removal, emits a `type=roll` GM-only log entry: `note=f"💀 {caster_name} lost concentration on {buff_name}{paired_note}"` + `breakdown=f"Concentration ends — {reason}"`. The caster name is read from `target.get("name")` (combatant display name, not character record). **(2)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_maybe_concentration_save` (the v2.49.48 0-HP forced-drop branch) — when `forced_drop_on_zero_hp=True`, switches emoji to 💀 and rewrites the breakdown to `"Concentration ends — incapacitated (0 HP) — save would have been 1d20[N]+M = X vs DC Y"`. The save text is preserved for telemetry so the GM can audit what the d20 was. **(3)** Both death-save callers now pass distinct reason strings: `roll_death_save` → `"3 failed death saves"`, `override_death_save` → `f"GM override → {status_in}"`. **(4)** `tests/harness/test_concentration_skull_log.py` (NEW, 4 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why a string ``reason`` param instead of an enum. The reason is purely human-readable log text — nothing downstream branches on it. An enum would force every caller to import + match on the value; a string lets each caller phrase the cause naturally and keeps `_drop_caster_concentration` agnostic to who's calling it. If a future commit needs structured cause data (e.g. for filtering the roll-log), the field can be added to the broadcast separately without rewriting the helper signature.
**Description (cont 2):** Why preserve the rolled save in the 0-HP breakdown. RAW says concentration ends regardless of the save outcome, but the d20 was still rolled (for parity with the existing broadcast contract — tests assert on `rolled`, `total`, `bonus`). The breakdown now reads "save would have been 1d20[18]+2 = 20 vs DC 10" — a passing roll, but RAW dropped concentration anyway. The GM can see at a glance whether the death was bad luck (failed both) or RAW-driven (would have passed but 0 HP). The 💀 emoji is the "this is RAW, not a dice failure" tell.
**Description (cont 3):** Why test_failed_con_save_still_emits_heart_log uses a retry loop. The non-0-HP CON save is genuinely random (d20 vs DC); to assert the 💔 log still appears, the test needs at least one failed save in the run. Rowan has no CON-save proficiency so P(fail | DC=15) ≈ 70%; 15 retries gives ~1 - 0.30^15 ≈ 99.999% chance of at least one failure. Same pattern as the existing v2.39.0 `test_concentration_break_emits_gm_only_log`.
**Description (cont 4):** Why test_roll_3_failures_emits_skull_log uses a retry loop instead of dice seeding. The TEST_MODE `/api/test/dice/seed` endpoint takes a single integer seed, not a forced d20 value. Finding a seed that produces three sub-DC rolls in a row is empirical + brittle to RNG implementation. Retry loop with 15 attempts (each: reset to dying/2-failures + re-hex + roll) has P(roll-fails | no-CON-prof) = 11/20 = 55%; ~99.99% chance of at least one death within 15 attempts. Reset overhead per loop is ~30ms (4 HTTP calls).
**Description (cont 5):** Verification. Ran the new tests pre-fix: `test_override_to_dead_emits_skull_log` failed (note started with 💔, breakdown said "✗ Failed" not "GM override"). Post-fix: all 4 pass. Full regression: 234 harness tests pass (was 230, +4 new); 33 encounter-sim tests still pass (no broadcast-shape break).

### Fixed
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_maybe_concentration_save` — when `forced_drop_on_zero_hp=True`, the GM roll-log entry now uses 💀 instead of 💔 and the breakdown names the cause ("incapacitated, 0 HP") instead of showing "✗ Failed" against a save that might have rolled a nat-20.

### Added
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_drop_caster_concentration` — accepts new keyword-only `reason` param; emits a 💀 GM-only roll-log entry per buff dropped, with paired-buff cascade summary mirrored from the v2.39.0 💔 log.
- `tests/harness/test_concentration_skull_log.py` — 4 tests covering 0-HP 💀 / failed-save 💔 (regression) / override-to-dead 💀 / roll-3-failures 💀 branches.
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry; total 230 → 234.

### Changed
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::roll_death_save` (death-save → dead branch) and `::override_death_save` (override → dying/stable/dead branches) now pass distinct `reason` strings to `_drop_caster_concentration` so the GM log entry names the cause.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure additive — broadcast shape unchanged. Clients that don't render the emoji distinction still receive the same `type=roll` event and can render the existing 💔 fallback path (matches all "lost concentration" notes). The 💀 emoji is a render-only difference today; clients can opt into a different visual style later.

### Filed
- **Knocked-out via non-damage incapacitation** — still open from v2.49.49. Sleep, hold person on the caster, banishment, etc. also incapacitate without dropping HP or failing a death save. Each condition-applying endpoint needs an audit to find which ones should also call `_drop_caster_concentration` with an appropriate reason string. Out of scope for this commit.
- **Concentration log emission on voluntary end** — `/end_buff` on a concentration buff currently emits only `buff_update`, no GM log. Voluntary ends are different from incapacitation but the GM still benefits from a one-line audit ("✋ Magnus ended concentration on Hex"). Could add a third emoji + reason variant in a future commit.

## [2.49.49] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Fix RAW bug: death-save state transitions didn't drop the caster's concentration.** Eighth application-side bug surfaced by the encounter-sim test suite. The v2.49.48 commit closed the 0-HP damage path (`_maybe_concentration_save` force-drops at 0 HP), but two adjacent endpoints sat outside that helper and still left concentration installed on dying / dead PCs: **(a)** `POST /character/{cid}/death-save` (rolling) — when a PC rolls 3 failures and dies, no damage event fires, no save runs through `_maybe_concentration_save`. **(b)** `POST /character/{cid}/death-save/override` — the GM force-sets status to dying / stable / dead with no damage or save. Both are real RAW gaps: PHB p.203 says concentration ends when the caster is incapacitated or killed regardless of how they got there. Fix: new `_drop_caster_concentration(campaign_id, character_id)` helper that scans the combatant's buffs for any with `concentration=True` and removes each via the existing `_remove_buff` cascade (which handles paired buff cleanup + sheet mirror + broadcast). Hooked into `roll_death_save` when `new_status == "dead"` and into `override_death_save` whenever the GM sets status to dying / stable / dead. 3 new harness tests pin both branches + a guard against over-broad firing on `status="alive"`. PATCH — bug fix; reuses the existing `buff_update` broadcast shape.
**Description:** Two edits. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py` — added `_drop_caster_concentration(campaign_id, character_id) -> int` helper near the existing `_drop_paired_concentration_buffs` cluster. It looks up the combatant by `char_id` in the live battle state, collects the keys of any buffs flagged `concentration: True`, and calls `_remove_buff` for each. Returns the count for telemetry / tests. Called from `roll_death_save` post-`_set_death_save_state` when the new status is "dead". Called from `override_death_save` whenever the incoming status is one of dying / stable / dead. **(2)** `tests/harness/test_death_save_drops_concentration.py` (NEW) — 3 tests: `test_override_to_dead_drops_concentration` (override(dead) on Hex'd Magnus → buff_update without hex + live /buffs confirms), `test_roll_3_failures_drops_concentration` (dying Magnus → override(failures=3, status=dead) → same broadcast assertion; uses override to drive the 3-failures transition deterministically since rolling three sub-DC d20s in a row needs careful seed selection), `test_override_to_alive_does_not_drop_concentration` (guard against over-broad fix — alive → alive transitions don't drop the buff).
**Description (cont):** Why two hook points, not one. The two endpoints share the underlying `_set_death_save_state` writer, but they take different paths INTO it: `roll_death_save` reads the current state, rolls a d20, decides the new status; `override_death_save` takes the status directly from the request body. Hooking into `_set_death_save_state` itself would be tempting (one site = fewer call sites to forget) but that helper is also called during the alive→alive idempotent path, and a top-down hook there would either over-fire (drop concentration when status doesn't actually change) or need a "did status transition?" check that duplicates the caller's logic. Cleaner to call the helper at the two endpoints where the transition has been COMMITTED and the new status is known.
**Description (cont 2):** Why `override(stable)` also drops. RAW: "stable" means the PC is unconscious at 0 HP but not actively dying — they're still incapacitated, so concentration ends. Pre-fix the override path could install Hex on an alive PC, then GM-override them to stable, and Hex would stay. The new firing condition is `status_in in ("dying", "stable", "dead")` covering all three incapacitated states; `status="alive"` is excluded so a healing override doesn't trigger unnecessary buff cleanup.
**Description (cont 3):** Why the rolled-3-failures test uses override(failures=3, status=dead) rather than rolling three d20s. Magnus has no CON-save proficiency so the death-save is raw 1d20 < 10. Forcing three sub-10 outcomes in a row through the dice-seed endpoint would need a specific seed sequence; the seed search is fiddly and brittle to dice-generator changes. The override path exercises the SAME `_drop_caster_concentration` code branch with deterministic input. The `roll_death_save` branch is itself covered indirectly because both endpoints route through the same helper — and `tests/harness/test_death_save.py` already pins the d20 mechanics.
**Description (cont 4):** Verification. Ran the new tests pre-fix: `test_override_to_dead_drops_concentration` failed at the `buff_update` assertion (no broadcast fired, hex stayed installed). Ran post-fix: all 3 pass. Full regression: 230 harness tests pass (was 227, +3 new); 33 encounter-sim tests pass (no regression). Eight bugs surfaced + fixed by encounter-sim so far.

### Fixed
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::roll_death_save` — when a death-save roll transitions the PC to status=dead, calls the new `_drop_caster_concentration` helper.
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::override_death_save` — when the override sets status to dying / stable / dead, calls `_drop_caster_concentration`.

### Added
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_drop_caster_concentration(campaign_id, character_id) -> int` — scans the live battle combatant for buffs flagged `concentration=True` and removes each via `_remove_buff`. Returns the count.
- `tests/harness/test_death_save_drops_concentration.py` — 3 tests covering the override(dead) branch, the rolled-3-failures branch (via override-driven status transition), and the override(alive) negative-control branch.
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry for the new test file; total 227 → 230.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure additive — reuses the existing `buff_update` broadcast shape (no new fields). Clients that already consume `buff_update` on buff removal will see hex / hunter's-mark / hold-person disappear from the buff list when the caster dies; that's the intended visible behavior.
- **Eight bugs fixed by encounter-sim so far**: v2.49.40 (force_gm_sync NPC damage), v2.49.41 (DELETE concentration paired-buffs), v2.49.42 (PATCH sheet-fields HP broadcast), v2.49.45 (hp_update handler renderBattle), v2.49.46 (death_save handler renderBattle), v2.49.47 (heal_applied handler renderBattle), v2.49.48 (RAW 0-HP concentration drop), v2.49.49 (this commit — death-save state transitions drop concentration).

## [2.49.48] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Fix RAW bug: concentration didn't end automatically at 0 HP.** Seventh application-side bug surfaced by the encounter-sim test suite. PHB p.203: "you also lose concentration on a spell if you are incapacitated or killed." Pre-fix, ``_maybe_concentration_save`` rolled the CON save unconditionally — a PC who took damage dropping to 0 HP could PASS the save and remain concentrating on Hex / Hunter's Mark / Hold Person / Spirit Guardians while dying or dead. The encounter-sim ``test_drops_on_zero_hp`` (v2.49.25) worked around this by inflating ``damage_amount`` to 65 (DC=32, impossible to pass) — the workaround documented the bug but didn't fix it. Fix: in ``_maybe_concentration_save``, snapshot the post-damage ``hp.current``; if it's 0 (or negative), force ``passed=False`` regardless of the d20 + add ``forced_drop_on_zero_hp: True`` to the broadcast for telemetry. The existing ``_remove_buff`` path runs, dropping the buff + cascading paired cleanup. The encounter-sim workaround can also drop the inflated damage back to a normal value — done in this commit. 2 new harness tests + 1 updated encounter-sim test pin both branches. PATCH — bug fix; the broadcast gains a ``forced_drop_on_zero_hp`` field (additive, defaults to False on the normal path).
**Description:** Three edits + 1 new file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_maybe_concentration_save` — snapshot ``hp.current`` after the existing damage application, compute ``forced_drop_on_zero_hp = hp_current_after <= 0``. Compute ``passed = (total >= dc) and not forced_drop_on_zero_hp``. Add the flag to the broadcast payload. The save is still ROLLED at 0 HP (kept for telemetry parity — the GM sees what the save WOULD have been) but the outcome is overridden. **(2)** `tests/harness/test_concentration_drops_on_zero_hp.py` (NEW) — 2 tests: (a) Magnus drops to 0 HP via damage_amount=15 (DC=10, passable); asserts ``forced_drop_on_zero_hp=True`` + ``passed=False`` + ``dropped_key="hex"``; (b) Magnus takes 13 damage to HP 20 (not 0); asserts ``forced_drop_on_zero_hp=False`` + ``passed`` follows the d20. **(3)** `tests/encounter_sim/level_3_edge_cases/concentration/test_drops_on_zero_hp.py` — damage tuning relaxed from 65 → 33 (full HP to 0) now that the forced-drop rule guarantees Hex drops without DC gymnastics. Comment captures the workaround history. **(4)** `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — new entry for the test file; total 225 → 227.
**Description (cont):** Why a new ``forced_drop_on_zero_hp`` field instead of just relying on ``passed=False``. Two reasons. (a) Telemetry / UX. The roll-log card currently renders "❌ Concentration save failed" on a fail. A 0-HP forced drop is conceptually different — the save WAS rolled and may have been a 20, but the rule says concentration ends regardless. Future UI can render "💀 Concentration broken (0 HP)" or similar, distinguished by the flag. (b) Backward compat. Existing client handlers + tests that only look at ``passed`` continue to behave correctly (the chip drops either way); the flag is purely additive metadata.
**Description (cont 2):** Why we still roll the d20 in the forced case. Could short-circuit and skip the roll, but rolling preserves the broadcast contract (existing tests assert on ``rolled``, ``total``, ``bonus`` fields) AND gives the GM auditable telemetry — "the save would have been a 19, but RAW dropped concentration anyway." Cost is one ``random.randint(1, 20)`` call per drop. Negligible.
**Description (cont 3):** How the encounter-sim suite surfaced this. ``test_drops_on_zero_hp`` (v2.49.25) was the first test that tried to assert "concentration drops on 0 HP." First write used damage_amount=33 (full HP → 0); the test was flaky because Magnus's CON+2 save sometimes passed against DC=16. The workaround was to inflate damage_amount to 65 (DC=32, unpassable). The CHANGELOG entry at v2.49.25 documented this as a tuning choice; this commit recognizes it as papering over a real RAW gap and fixes the underlying rule. With the fix, damage_amount=33 works deterministically — the test was simplified back to that value.
**Description (cont 4):** Verification. Ran the new harness tests pre-fix: ``test_concentration_force_drops_at_zero_hp`` failed (concentration was rolled, ``passed`` could be True). Ran post-fix: both pass. 227 harness tests pass (was 225, +2 new); 33 encounter-sim tests pass with the simplified damage value.

### Fixed
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_maybe_concentration_save` — force-drops concentration when caster's HP is 0 (RAW PHB p.203). Adds ``forced_drop_on_zero_hp`` field to the ``concentration_save`` broadcast.

### Added
- `tests/harness/test_concentration_drops_on_zero_hp.py` — 2 tests covering the forced-drop branch + the normal-save branch.

## [2.49.45] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Fix bug #4 from encounter-sim: `character_hp_update` handler didn't refresh the init tracker — PC HP drops stayed visually stale.** Fourth application-side bug surfaced by the encounter-sim test suite. Pre-fix: when a PC took damage (or was healed), the server broadcast `character_hp_update`; the client's handler in `tabletop.js:3102` mutated `window.battle.combatants[…].hp_current` AND called the canvas `render()` AND called `_updateMiniHpDisplay` (which updates the mini-sheet card's HP line) — but never triggered `renderBattle()` to repaint the init tracker's `.mini-header-sub` "HP X / Y" text. So a PC who took damage showed correct HP everywhere EXCEPT the init tracker's mini-header line, which stayed at the pre-damage value until something else (turn advance, manual edit) caused a renderBattle pass. NPC-damage takes a different broadcast path (`battle_update`) which DOES call renderBattle, so the bug was PC-only. Surfaced by the encounter-sim `test_alice_observes_hp_update` after the v2.49.42 PATCH /sheet-fields broadcast fix landed: with the broadcast finally working, the test could SEE that the DOM didn't update. Fix: expose `renderBattle` on `window._renderBattle` from the tabletop.html IIFE; call it from `_onCharacterHpUpdate` in tabletop.js right after `render()`. Also simplifies the Alice test from the now-obsolete /attack-with-seeded-dice-retry pattern to a direct `apply_damage` PATCH. PATCH — bug fix; no schema or API contract change.
**Description:** Three edits. **(1)** `app/templates/tabletop.html` — added `window._renderBattle = renderBattle;` right after the `renderBattle` definition (line ~5282). Mirrors the pattern at line 2905 (`window._openDrawerPanel = openPanel`) — the IIFE-local functions that need to be reachable from `tabletop.js` get exposed via `window.*`. Comment cites the v2.49.45 fix context. **(2)** `app/static/tabletop.js::_onCharacterHpUpdate` (line ~3119) — after the existing `render()` call, added `if (typeof window._renderBattle === 'function') { try { window._renderBattle(); } catch (_) {} }`. The try/catch matches the existing pattern (canvas render can throw if there's no active map). **(3)** `tests/encounter_sim/level_3_edge_cases/multi_user/test_alice_observes_hp_update.py` — rewrote from the /attack-with-Krieger-and-seeded-dice pattern to a direct `apply_damage(pip, damage_amount=10, new_hp_current=25)` PATCH. Removed Krieger from the seed, removed set_auto_apply, removed set_dice_seed + retry-on-miss. Test is now 10 lines shorter, fully deterministic, and exercises THE EXACT bug class (PC damage via PATCH → broadcast → DOM update).
**Description (cont):** Why this bug class is subtle. Three independent code paths fire on damage: the canvas re-render (window.render or local render in tabletop.js), the mini-sheet card update (_updateMiniHpDisplay updates `.mini-stat-row[data-char-id]`), and the init-tracker re-render (renderBattle updates `.init-entry > .mini-header-sub`). The hp_update handler called the first two but not the third. In manual GM testing the GM would either be looking at the canvas (where the skull overlay shows on 0 HP — fixed in v2.49.4) or the mini-sheet card (where HP shows correctly) — both consistent with the bug being invisible. The init tracker mini-header was the one place where stale HP rendered.
**Description (cont 2):** Why no new harness test. This bug is purely client-side (the broadcast was already correct in shape and content per the v2.49.42 fix). The harness suite tests broadcast contracts; no harness test can verify "the JS handler called renderBattle." The encounter-sim test_alice_observes_hp_update IS the regression test — it observes Alice's DOM, which only updates correctly with the fix in place. Pre-fix, the test would fail at the post-PATCH DOM assertion (verified — the test was failing before the fix).
**Description (cont 3):** Why this fix completes the encounter-sim feedback loop. The bug class — broadcast correct but DOM render broken — is EXACTLY the regression class that motivated the encounter-sim suite (the v2.49.4 skull overlay). v2.49.42 fixed the broadcast SIDE of HP changes via PATCH; v2.49.45 fixes the RENDER SIDE for the init tracker. The suite caught it. The test simplification is the bonus: now that PATCH broadcasts work, the player-driver observation test doesn't need the dice-retry workaround.

### Fixed
- `app/templates/tabletop.html` — exposes `window._renderBattle` after the `renderBattle` function definition.
- `app/static/tabletop.js::_onCharacterHpUpdate` — now calls `window._renderBattle()` after the canvas `render()`. Closes the PC-damage-stale-init-tracker bug.

### Changed
- `tests/encounter_sim/level_3_edge_cases/multi_user/test_alice_observes_hp_update.py` — simplified from /attack-with-seeded-dice-retry to a direct PATCH `/sheet-fields` flow. ~10 lines shorter, fully deterministic, exercises the exact v2.49.45 bug class. Test history captured in the docstring.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure additive client fix — exposing a function on window + adding a call. Existing handlers / tests / clients unaffected.
- **Bug-pair**: v2.49.42 (broadcast fix) + v2.49.45 (render fix) together close the loop on PC HP changes via PATCH. Either alone is insufficient; together they make the path work end-to-end.

### Filed
- **Survey other broadcast handlers in `tabletop.js`** for the same missing-renderBattle pattern. character_death_save handler at line 3136 mutates death-save tracker DOM but doesn't call renderBattle either — if a status change shifts HP (e.g. healing word reviving Pip), the init-tracker HP-bar could similarly stale. Worth a defensive renderBattle call.

All 3 server-initiated paths now broadcast with `force_gm_sync: True`. **Description:** Four edits. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_install_buff_on_combatant_id` (line 543) — broadcast now carries `force_gm_sync: True`. Fixes the case where an NPC buff (Paralyzed from Hold Person, Frightened from Fear) is installed but the GM's view of the chip doesn't update until the next push. **(2)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_drop_paired_concentration_buffs` (line 745) — same fix. When concentration ends and paired target-side conditions drop, the GM sees the cleanup immediately. **(3)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_apply_heal_to_combatant` NPC branch (line 1262) — same fix for the heal path. **Description (cont):** Why PUT /battle (line 12907) correctly omits the flag. PUT /battle is the GM-initiated push path — the GM's client calls `pushBattle()` to send their local state up to the server, the server stores it, then broadcasts to OTHER clients. If this broadcast had `force_gm_sync: True`, the GM would immediately receive their own push back, mid-edit, and the echo-loop guard at tabletop.html:5543 wouldn't help. The flag is exactly the discriminator for "server-computed state change" (force the GM to apply it) vs "GM-pushed state change" (let the GM's local copy be authoritative). All 4 broadcasts now classified correctly.

The contract being tested is `force_gm_sync: True` on `battle_update` broadcasts, which v2.49.40's `test_npc_damage_broadcast_carries_force_gm_sync` already asserts for one path. The 3 additional broadcast sites fixed here all use the same pattern. Adding 3 more nearly-identical tests would be low-value duplication; the principle (server-side state mutations carry the flag) is sufficient documented + tested once. Filed: a parametrized audit test that asserts every server-side broadcast has the flag, if drift becomes a concern.
**Description (cont 3):** Verification. 225 harness tests pass (was 225, no new tests added); 32 encounter-sim tests pass. The flaky `test_attack_sneak_attack_uplift` failure that was occasionally surfacing under the v2.49.40 changes is now consistent — failures dropped from ~3/5 runs (pre-audit) to ~1/5 runs (post-audit + teardown). The settings page submits PATCH /sheet-fields with the full sheet body on every save — even unrelated edits like "rename a feat" arrive with `hp: {current: 35}` because the form serializer doesn't know which fields changed. Without the no-op suppression, every settings save would spam `character_hp_update` to every client. The `new_current != pre_patch_current_hp` guard kills the spam path; only ACTUAL HP changes fire the broadcast.
**Description (cont 3):** Verification. Ran the new tests BEFORE the fix landed (all 3 failed — no broadcast); ran AFTER (all 3 pass). 225 harness tests pass; 32 encounter-sim tests still pass (no regressions). The encounter-sim `test_alice_observes_hp_update` could now use PATCH /sheet-fields instead of /attack as its damage trigger; not refactored in this commit (the existing test still validates the broadcast → DOM path the same way), but filed as cleanup.

### Fixed
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::patch_sheet_fields` — broadcasts `character_hp_update` on HP change (not just `character_death_save` on status crossings). Non-GM clients now observe HP-bar movement from GM sheet edits, in-test PATCHes, and anywhere else this endpoint mutates HP within "alive".

### Added
- `tests/harness/test_sheet_patch_hp_broadcast.py` — 3 tests pinning the new broadcast contract:
  - `test_hp_drop_within_alive_broadcasts` — HP down without status crossing fires the broadcast with negative delta.
  - `test_hp_heal_broadcasts_positive_delta` — HP up fires with positive delta.
  - `test_hp_unchanged_does_not_broadcast` — no-op PATCH (settings-form spam guard) suppresses the broadcast.

### Changed
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — new catalog entry; total tests 222 → 225.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure additive — `character_hp_update` is an existing message type with an existing client handler; this commit just causes it to fire in more places. Clients that don't handle the message continue to work (they did before too).
- **Settings-form spam.** Verified the no-op suppression with the `test_hp_unchanged_does_not_broadcast` test. Without that guard, every GM settings-page save would broadcast `character_hp_update` to every client — measurable performance impact at scale.

### Filed
- **Refactor `test_alice_observes_hp_update` to use PATCH /sheet-fields**. Currently uses /attack with a seeded-dice hit retry; PATCH would be simpler + always-deterministic + would exercise this new fix path end-to-end.
- **Survey OTHER `_apply_hp_change` call sites** for the same missing-broadcast pattern. Most paths (attack, heal) broadcast via their own helpers; double-check that no other "set HP directly" path is silent.
- **Three bugs surfaced + fixed by the encounter-sim suite so far** (v2.49.40 / v2.49.41 / v2.49.42). The suite is paying for itself.

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Fix bug #2 from encounter-sim: `DELETE /concentration` left buffs on the caster + targets.** Second application-side bug surfaced by the encounter-sim test suite (after v2.49.40's force_gm_sync fix). Pre-fix: `DELETE /api/campaign/{cid}/concentration/{char_id}` deleted the `ConcentrationEffect` DB row and broadcast `concentration_update` with `ended: True` — but left the caster-side concentration buff (Hex / Hunter's Mark / etc.) on the caster's `combatant.buffs` list AND left paired target-side conditions (Paralyzed from Hold Person, Frightened from Fear, …) on every affected target.
